motivation: GDP and zCDP are competing privacy accounting frameworks with similar minimax lower bounds, but only one direction of conversion was known at the same calibration, leaving the reverse conversion and the source of their asymptotic equivalence unclear.
method: The authors derive an optimal zCDP-to-GDP conversion by solving a defining equation for the GDP parameter, prove sharp simplified bounds with explicit constants, and analyze convexity of the squared conversion to determine ordering effects under composition and group privacy.
result: Every zCDP mechanism is shown to satisfy GDP with an optimally calibrated parameter, the two frameworks are equivalent up to constants, and converting zCDP to GDP before composition or group privacy can yield tighter guarantees than converting afterward.
conclusion: The work closes the reverse conversion gap between zCDP and GDP and explains their matching minimax risks via constant rescaling of the privacy budget, with practical implications for privacy accounting order.

title: Enhancing Edge Ai System Security With A Stacked Hardware Security Controller For Robust And Energy-Efficient Anomaly Detectio
authors: Carl Benda, Eren Kurshan, Paul Franzon
abstract: ArXiv:2611.01150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, the growing adoption of Edge AI systems has been accompanied by a surge in security threats. Edge AI deployments face an rapidly evolving spectrum of security threats, from side-channel information leakage to ad- versarial model manipulation and physical device tampering. Conventional security mechanisms such as malware scanners and resource-intensive firewall solutions are unsuitable due to edge AIs typically limited computational resources, strict energy budgets and thermal constraints especially in battery-powered and field-deployed environments. This paper proposes a stacked, hardware-based security mechanism that enables low-overhead, continuous detection of anomalous execution patterns. Anomaly detection utilizing hard- ware performance counters and physical sensors outperforms software-based alternatives by providing key capabilities such as tamper-resistant root-of-trust isolation, negligible runtime overhead, and resilience against compromised operating systems. Experimental analysis shows that adversarial or malicious ap- plications produce observable deviations in sensor and thermal readings on Edge AI systems and hardware-based anomaly detection provides effective and low-overhead anomaly detection.
tldr: The paper proposes a stacked hardware-based security controller using performance counters and physical sensors to detect anomalous execution in Edge AI systems with low energy overhead.
motivation: Edge AI deployments face security threats ranging from side-channel leakage to adversarial model manipulation, but conventional software security tools are too resource- and energy-intensive for constrained edge hardware.
method: The authors design a stacked hardware security mechanism that continuously monitors hardware performance counters and physical/thermal sensors, using deviations in these readings as signatures of adversarial or malicious applications.
result: Experiments show that malicious applications produce observable deviations in sensor and thermal readings, enabling effective low-overhead hardware-based anomaly detection.
conclusion: Hardware-assisted anomaly detection offers a tamper-resistant, low-latency alternative to software security for Edge AI, though the work is engineering-focused with no quantum information or thermodynamic content.

title: HideOut - User Protection Against Localization With Throughput Guarantees In Mobile Networks
authors: Navidreza Asadi, Michele Guardiani, Wolfgang Kellerer, Jafar Aco Mohammadi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Channel state information (CSI) in cellular networks is primarily used to maintain quality of service (QoS), yet it leaks privacy-sensitive information, in particular the user equipment's (UE) location. CSI is reported in plaintext on a publicly available schedule; thus, capturing it on the air and using a well trained AI model to localize the UE is straightforward. This simplicity in the attack execution makes it a serious privacy vulnerability. Using conventional privacy enhancing techniques, such as additive perturbation from differential privacy, to protect location data can potentially degrade the downlink communication quality. We present HideOut, a client-side defense mechanism that preserves the user's location from neural-based localization methods, while maintaining their downlink Spectral Efficiency (SE). Unlike generic adversarial attacks, HideOut treats downlink SE as a strict constraint in an optimization setting. Under maximum ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming, we show that a user-selected SE loss budget can be converted into an angular rate-feasible constraint on the reported channel vector. HideOut then performs gradient-based localization obfuscation while projecting each update onto this rate-feasible set. We evaluate HideOut against four CSI-based localization architectures under both white-box and black-box assumptions. Across models, HideOut increases localization ambiguity (error) from approximately [MATH] m to [MATH] m while keeping downlink SE loss within a [MATH] budget. These results show that CSI-based localization can be substantially degraded at negligible communication quality loss when adversarial perturbations are made aware of the wireless link.
tldr: HideOut is a client-side defense that obfuscates CSI-based localization in mobile networks while constraining downlink spectral efficiency loss.
motivation: Channel state information reported in cellular networks leaks user location and can be exploited by AI-based localization, but conventional privacy methods may degrade communication quality.
method: The authors formulate localization obfuscation as an optimization problem under an MRT beamforming model, converting an SE loss budget into an angular rate-feasible constraint and applying gradient-based projected perturbations to reported channel vectors.
result: Against four CSI-based localization architectures in white-box and black-box settings, HideOut increases localization error substantially while keeping downlink SE loss within a small user-selected budget.
conclusion: The work shows that CSI-based localization can be degraded with negligible communication quality loss when adversarial perturbations respect wireless link constraints.

title: Loss Of Monotonicity In The Vector Play Model And Consequences For Newton-Type Solvers
authors: Dominik Cibicki, Klaus Roppert, Manfred Kaltenbacher
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The vector play model (VPM) replaces the implicit minimization of the energy-based hysteresis model (EBM) by an explicit update. Its tangent contains the product of the Hessians of two unrelated potentials and is unsymmetric. Hence, the VPM has no co-energy density at frozen memory, and the skew part makes [MATH] lose monotonicity in a band just outside the pinning circle, into which small time steps drive the sliding states. In composite models, the determinant of the tangent can change sign, which explains published failures of the local inversion [MATH], and where it is negative, [MATH] is not injective. In the scalar potential formulation, the exact tangent keeps a descent guarantee, whereas symmetric surrogates of the tangent, such as the symmetrized tangent or Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) updates, lose it and become ascent directions where the skew part dominates, as computations of TEAM Problem 32 confirm. It is therefore recommended to use solvers with an unsymmetric tangent.
tldr: The paper analyzes loss of monotonicity in the vector play model for hysteresis and its consequences for Newton-type solvers.
motivation: The vector play model is used as an explicit alternative to energy-based hysteresis models, but its unsymmetric tangent can break monotonicity and cause solver failures.
method: The authors examine the tangent of the vector play model, show that it contains products of Hessians of unrelated potentials, and study monotonicity and injectivity in scalar and composite formulations.
result: They find that the skew part destroys monotonicity in a band outside the pinning circle, that composite-model tangents can change sign, and that symmetric surrogates such as BFGS can produce ascent directions.
conclusion: The authors recommend using Newton-type solvers that retain the unsymmetric tangent rather than symmetrized or quasi-Newton approximations.

title: A Note On The NP-Hardness On Quadratic Optimization Over Doubly Stochastic Matrices And The Gromov-Wasserstein Problem
authors: Yong Sheng Soh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Gromov-Wasserstein problem is an extension of the regular optimal transport problem that is adapted for pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. Broadly speaking, given a pair of metric measure spaces, the Gromov-Wasserstein problem seeks couplings between these spaces that minimize the distortion between the metric evaluations. In this note we record the fact that the Gromov-Wasserstein distance between finite metric spaces is NP-Hard to compute. Our argument relies on a reduction from the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem, and it builds on ideas in Vayer's thesis and Ryner et. al's work that draw connections between the 2-Gromov-Wasserstein and the Quadratic Assignment Problem. During the preparation of this manuscript we learned of the appearance of Breitung et. al's work, whose result essentially supersedes ours. We hope this note serves as a useful companion whose proof is, hopefully, more elementary and easier to understand.
tldr: This note proves that computing the Gromov-Wasserstein distance between finite metric spaces is NP-hard via a reduction from the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem.
motivation: The Gromov-Wasserstein distance extends optimal transport to incomparable metric measure spaces, but its computational complexity had not been settled in a simple, self-contained way.
method: A reduction from the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem to the 2-Gromov-Wasserstein problem, building on connections to the Quadratic Assignment Problem and quadratic optimization over doubly stochastic matrices as developed in Vayer's thesis and Ryner et al.
result: The Gromov-Wasserstein distance between finite metric spaces is shown to be NP-hard to compute, though the authors note that a concurrent work by Breitung et al. supersedes this result.
conclusion: The note is offered as an elementary, accessible companion proof of NP-hardness for Gromov-Wasserstein, though its contribution is largely subsumed by prior concurrent work.

title: Unconditional Optimal Convergence Of A Relaxation Crank-Nicolson Difference Scheme For 2d Space-fractional Nls
authors: Dongling Wang Lisen Ding
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a linearly implicit relaxation Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for the two-dimensional space-fractional nonlinear Schr\"odinger (SFNS) equation, where the fractional Laplacian is approximated by a simple fractional central difference scheme. The proposed scheme is uniquely solvable and conserves discrete mass for general real-valued nonlinear coefficients, and a modified discrete energy in the cubic case. By introducing a modified error system employing a cut-off technique, we establish the optimal-order error estimates without mesh-ratio restriction. Specifically, the primary variable achieves second-order temporal and spatial convergence in the discrete [MATH]-norm, and the relaxation variable satisfies the same convergence in the discrete [MATH]-norm. Some numerical experiments confirm the relevant theoretical results.

motivation: Space-fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equations require numerical schemes that are stable, conservative, and free of restrictive mesh-ratio constraints, which existing methods often fail to guarantee.
method: A fractional central difference approximation of the fractional Laplacian is combined with a relaxation Crank-Nicolson time discretization; a modified error system with a cut-off technique is introduced to derive error estimates.
result: The scheme is uniquely solvable, conserves discrete mass (and a modified discrete energy in the cubic case), and achieves second-order convergence in both time and space in discrete L2 norms for the primary and relaxation variables without mesh-ratio restrictions.
conclusion: Theoretical results are confirmed by numerical experiments, establishing the scheme as an efficient and unconditionally convergent approach for 2D space-fractional NLS equations.

title: A Complete Classification For N-species Lotka-Volterra Stably Dissipative Systems Based On A Generalized Ahu Algorithm
authors: Yajia Du, Zhengyi Lu, Jinya Xu, Ming Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a generalized AHU algorithm based on tree isomorphism theory and applies it to the complete classification of n-dimensional stably dissipative Lotka-Volterra systems.

motivation: Stably dissipative Lotka-Volterra systems admit a rich but incompletely understood classification; existing case-by-case analyses do not scale to n species, motivating a systematic algorithmic approach.
method: The authors build on tree isomorphism theory from graph/computer-science algorithms, generalizing the AHU canonical-labeling procedure, and apply it to the combinatorial structure of Lotka-Volterra interaction graphs.
result: A complete classification of n-species stably dissipative Lotka-Volterra systems is obtained via the generalized algorithm, providing a canonical, computable invariant for the equivalence classes.
conclusion: The generalized AHU approach yields a systematic classification scheme for stably dissipative Lotka-Volterra systems, and the algorithmic viewpoint may transfer to other structured dynamical systems.

title: A Second-Order Stochastic Dynamic Mode Decomposition By Richardson Extrapolation
authors: Yuanchao Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic dynamic mode decomposition (SDMD) approximates the Koopman semigroup of an It\^o diffusion by a Galerkin generator matrix on a dictionary of observables, computed from samples of the invariant law and evaluations of the generator, and advances observables with a first-order stochastic Taylor step (SDMD-1). title: Univalent Non-Associative Categorical Structures
authors: Beatrice Szilvasy
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study category-like structures in which composition is not associative, especially Munch-Maccagnoni's duploids, in univalent foundations. Included is a definition of what a univalent duploid is: one where isomorphisms of a suitable kind render the objects indistinguishable to the type theory. We show that the existing construction of a duploid from an adjunction is not univalent as a "single-sorted" duploid, and provide a novel construction which is. This work is formalized in the UniMath library for the Rocq proof assistant.
tldr: The paper studies univalent foundations for non-associative categorical structures, specifically duploids, and provides a univalent construction from adjunctions formalized in UniMath.
motivation: Duploids model category-like structures with non-associative composition, but their treatment in univalent foundations has not been developed, particularly regarding when such structures are univalent.
method: The author defines univalent duploids, shows that the standard construction from an adjunction fails to be univalent as a single-sorted duploid, and introduces a novel univalent construction, formalizing the results in the UniMath library for Rocq.
result: A new construction of a univalent duploid from an adjunction is given, overcoming the non-univalence of the existing single-sorted construction.
conclusion: The work advances the formalization of non-associative categorical structures in univalent type theory, with implications for proof assistants and categorical semantics.

tldr: The paper presents practical preimage attacks on reduced-round (19- and 20-step) SHA-256 that respect the standard IV, Davies-Meyer feed-forward, and full FIPS 180-4 padding for arbitrary 256-bit targets.
motivation: Reduced-round SHA-256 preimage attacks with proper padding constraints are rare, and demonstrating feasible attacks on 19-20 steps helps calibrate the security margin of the full 64-step function.

title: Adversarial Robustness Is Not Zero-Day Generalization: A Controlled Evaluation Of Flow-Based Intrusion Detectors On Corrected Cic-ids2017
authors: Abdulhamid Zaro
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic variants of known attacks, including feature-space adversarial perturbations, are sometimes used as stand-ins for unseen ("zero-day") attacks when evaluating machine-learning network intrusion detection systems (NIDS). We test whether this proxy holds. On the corrected CIC-IDS2017 release we train Random Forest, XGBoost, a 1D-CNN and an FT-Transformer and compare, at a fixed 1% false-positive rate over five seeds, detection under constrained perturbations of known attacks (gradient-based and black-box attacks on 42 attacker-controllable features) with leave-one-attack-family-out (LOAO) detection, where an entire family is absent from training. Detection under the strongest perturbation we tested, with budgets of at most 0.2, stays between 90.9% and 99.7%, yet mean detection of held-out families falls to 76.2% (RF), 40.2% (XGBoost), 25.8% (1D-CNN) and 22.8% (FT-Transformer). Robustness exceeds LOAO detection for every model (gaps of 24 to 72 percentage points, 23 to 66 when robustness is also averaged over families; Holm-adjusted p [MATH] 0.00096), and the two measures agree at most on a coarse ranking of the models. An exact mixed-integer evasion search confirms the tree ensembles' scores. Benign-only anomaly detectors and a simple multi-class open-set baseline do not close the gap. A temporal split on 5 seeds (3 of the 4 models) leaves the gap in place. On CSE-CIC-IDS2018 the gap recurs for every model (16 to 68 points). On these benchmarks and under this threat model, a robustness score should not be read as a zero-day score, and the two should be reported separately. Code and per-seed results are publicly available.
tldr: This paper evaluates whether adversarial robustness of machine-learning network intrusion detectors is a valid proxy for zero-day attack generalization on corrected CIC-IDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 benchmarks.
motivation: Synthetic adversarial variants of known attacks are often used as stand-ins for unseen zero-day attacks when assessing ML-based network intrusion detection systems, but the validity of this proxy is unclear.
method: The authors train Random Forest, XGBoost, a 1D-CNN, and an FT-Transformer, then compare detection under constrained feature-space perturbations of known attacks with leave-one-attack-family-out detection at a fixed 1% false-positive rate over five seeds.
result: Robustness scores remain high (90.9%–99.7%) under strong perturbations, while held-out attack-family detection drops sharply (76.2% RF, 40.2% XGBoost, 25.8% 1D-CNN, 22.8% FT-Transformer), with gaps of 24–72 percentage points that persist across temporal splits and CSE-CIC-IDS2018.
conclusion: On these benchmarks and under the considered threat model, adversarial robustness should not be interpreted as zero-day generalization; the two measures should be reported separately.

title: Martingalized U-statistics-based Sequential Inference: A Blessing Of Degeneracy
authors: Weijia Li, Leheng Cai, Qirui Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Degenerate degree-two U-statistics have non-Gaussian limits, making sequential inference substantially more difficult than in the nondegenerate case. However, row normalization preserves the target parameter and makes the centered numerator a martingale on a harmonic variance clock, at the cost of logarithmic variance inflation. We establish a strong Gaussian approximation for this process and consistently estimate its variance through online updates, allowing spectrum-free calibration. Combining this strong approximation with Gaussian-mixture (GM) and stitched law-of-the-iterated-logarithm (LIL) boundaries yields confidence sequences with asymptotic time-uniform coverage and corresponding sequential tests for null hypotheses under which the kernel is degenerate. We further extend the framework to multi-dimensional vector-valued kernels, yielding Mahalanobis confidence ellipsoids based on consistent covariance estimation. Numerical experiments illustrate sequential type-I error control and favorable detection power in two-sample and independence testing against spectral baselines, and in three-sample homogeneity testing using vector confidence ellipsoids.
tldr: The paper develops martingale-based sequential inference for degenerate degree-two U-statistics, constructing confidence sequences and sequential tests with time-uniform coverage.
motivation: Degenerate U-statistics have non-Gaussian limit distributions, which makes sequential (anytime-valid) inference much harder than in the nondegenerate case, so a new calibration technique is needed.
method: Row normalization is applied to turn the centered statistic into a martingale on a harmonic variance clock, a strong Gaussian approximation is established, variances are estimated online, and Gaussian-mixture plus stitched LIL boundaries yield confidence sequences; the framework is extended to vector-valued kernels via Mahalanobis ellipsoids.
result: The confidence sequences attain asymptotic time-uniform coverage, with numerical experiments showing type-I error control and competitive detection power in two-sample, independence, and three-sample homogeneity testing compared with spectral baselines.
conclusion: Degeneracy can be exploited as an advantage for sequential nonparametric inference, giving spectrum-free, anytime-valid procedures that extend to multivariate kernels.

title: FIXP-Completeness In Second-Price Auctions
authors: Nobutaka Shimizu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing equilibria is a fundamental algorithmic problem in game theory and economics. Although general frameworks are available for proving membership in FIXP, the class capturing exact fixed-point computation, establishing FIXP-completeness often remains challenging. We prove FIXP-completeness of exact equilibrium computation in three second-price auction models: (1). pacing with return-on-investment constraints, with multiplier cap [MATH] for every fixed rational [MATH] [Filos-Ratsikas, Hansen, H{\o}gh, and Hollender (2024)]; (2). budget-constrained generalized second-price sponsored shopping [Hansen, Li, and Nie (2026)]; (3). budget-constrained throttling [Liu (2026)]. These results resolve open questions on the exact complexity of automated bidding. Our technical ingredient is a FIXP-complete generalized-circuit problem using only clipped affine gates and the reciprocal [MATH], for any fixed positive rational [MATH]. This gate basis provides a common framework for the three auction reductions: simulating these gates in each model establishes FIXP-hardness without directly implementing multiplication or squaring.
tldr: The paper proves FIXP-completeness of exact equilibrium computation in three second-price auction models (pacing with ROI constraints, budget-constrained generalized second-price sponsored shopping, and budget-constrained throttling).
motivation: Computing equilibria is a fundamental algorithmic problem, and while membership in FIXP is often provable via general frameworks, establishing FIXP-completeness for concrete auction models has remained difficult; several open questions on the exact complexity of automated bidding are resolved here.
method: The authors introduce a FIXP-complete generalized-circuit problem built only from clipped affine gates and the reciprocal function, then reduce this gate basis into each of the three auction models to obtain FIXP-hardness without directly implementing multiplication or squaring.
result: All three second-price auction equilibrium problems are shown to be FIXP-complete for any fixed rational cap, yielding a common reduction framework across the models.
conclusion: The work settles open complexity questions for automated bidding equilibria and provides a reusable clipped-affine-plus-reciprocal gate basis for future FIXP-completeness reductions.

title: A $\theta$-implicit Hybrid Particle-in-cell Algorithm For Kinetic Simulations Of Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Prabhat Kumar, William J. White, Stephen E. Clark
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid particle-in-cell (PIC) models with kinetic ions and an inertialess electron fluid are widely used to simulate magnetized plasmas at ion scales, but explicit time advances are constrained by the whistler-wave CFL condition [MATH], and the sub-cycling and artificial dissipation used to mitigate it carry accumulating costs. We present a [MATH]-implicit hybrid PIC algorithm, implemented in the open-source GPU-capable code WarpX, in which fields and particles are advanced as a single nonlinear system solved by a particle-suppressed Jacobian-free Newton--Krylov method: the particles are nonlinearly eliminated, the electric field of the generalized Ohm's law is the sole unknown, and mass matrices remove all particle operations from the linear iterations. The electron pressure is advanced inside the nonlinear solve, and the scheme satisfies a discrete energy law whose single dissipation term vanishes at [MATH] and damps only temporally under-resolved modes for [MATH]. The advance reproduces parallel and perpendicular wave dispersion including the ion Bernstein modes, conserves total energy to machine roundoff where the explicit advance heats secularly, does not develop the cold-beam finite-grid instability, and reproduces the [MATH] instability of a Bennett pinch in RZ geometry. We conclude with 3D simulations of a field-reversed configuration initialized from a Grad--Shafranov equilibrium, comparing the explicit and implicit advances on the growth of the tilt instability and the preservation of trapped magnetic flux.

motivation: Explicit hybrid PIC advances are constrained by the whistler-wave CFL condition, and sub-cycling or artificial dissipation used to circumvent this incur accumulating costs and numerical artifacts.
method: Fields and particles are advanced as a single nonlinear system solved with a particle-suppressed Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov scheme, eliminating particles nonlinearly and using an electric field from the generalized Ohm's law as the sole unknown, with mass matrices removing particle operations from linear iterations.
result: The scheme satisfies a discrete energy law, reproduces parallel and perpendicular wave dispersion including ion Bernstein modes, conserves energy to roundoff, avoids the cold-beam finite-grid instability, and reproduces the m=1 instability of a Bennett pinch in RZ geometry, with 3D field-reversed configuration simulations comparing implicit and explicit advances.
conclusion: The θ-implicit hybrid PIC approach offers a robust, energy-conserving alternative to explicit advances for magnetized plasma simulations at ion scales, mitigating CFL constraints and numerical instabilities.

title: A Representation Theorem For Fractional Viscoelastic Networks
authors: Andrea Giusti, Ivano Colombaro, Andrea Mentrelli, Francesco Mainardi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a representation theorem for finite series-parallel viscoelastic networks composed of springs and spring-pots of a common order [MATH]. The associated complex shear modulus, expressed in an appropriately chosen auxiliary variable, is rational and admits a finite partial-fraction representation with simple poles on the negative real axis and negative residues. Its reciprocal admits an analogous representation with positive residues and a possible additional pole at the origin. Inverting the corresponding Laplace transforms gives finite fractional Prony representations of the relaxation modulus and creep compliance with non-negative amplitudes. These results provide a rigorous proof of a corrected version of the Mainardi-Spada conjecture for this network class. A six-element network illustrates the construction.
tldr: The paper proves a representation theorem showing that finite series-parallel networks of springs and fractional spring-pots admit rational shear moduli with partial-fraction expansions, yielding fractional Prony representations of relaxation and creep with non-negative amplitudes.
motivation: Fractional viscoelastic models (spring-pots) are widely used to fit rheological data, but rigorous justification for the associated Prony-type spectral representations, and in particular a corrected form of the Mainardi-Spada conjecture, was lacking for finite series-parallel networks.
method: The authors work in an auxiliary variable in which the complex shear modulus of a series-parallel network of common-order spring-pots becomes rational, then use partial-fraction decomposition and Laplace inversion to obtain relaxation and creep representations; a six-element network serves as an illustrative example.
result: The modulus has simple poles on the negative real axis with negative residues, its reciprocal has positive residues plus possibly a pole at the origin, and both relaxation modulus and creep compliance admit finite fractional Prony series with non-negative amplitudes, proving the corrected conjecture.
conclusion: The theorem places fractional viscoelastic network modeling on a rigorous footing and guarantees physically admissible (non-negative amplitude) Prony representations for this network class.

title: Energy-Efficient Uav Covert Communications Via Metaheuristic Optimization
authors: Nguyen Minh Quan, Tran Thanh Thu, Nguyen The Ngoc Khue, Ninh Thi Thanh Tam, Trinh van Chien
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wireless communication systems increasingly require not only confidentiality but also transmission undetectability, motivating covert communications. This paper studies an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) enabled covert communication system where a UAV serves a legitimate receiver in the presence of multiple active and colluding wardens with imperfect location information. We maximize covert energy efficiency (CEE) by jointly optimizing the UAV's 3D trajectory and transmit power while accounting for energy. To address the resulting non-convex problem with robust covertness constraints, we develop Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)-based metaheuristic algorithms and compare them with a Block Coordinate Descent with Successive Convex Approximation (BCD-SCA) benchmark. Numerical results show that the proposed methods improve CEE while satisfying covertness constraints.
tldr: The paper optimizes 3D trajectory and transmit power of a UAV for covert communication energy efficiency in the presence of colluding wardens using genetic algorithms and particle swarm optimization.
motivation: Wireless systems increasingly demand not only confidentiality but also transmission undetectability, motivating covert communications; UAVs offer mobility advantages but energy efficiency under robust covertness constraints is challenging.
method: The authors formulate a non-convex covert energy efficiency maximization with imperfect warden location information and solve it with GA and PSO metaheuristics, benchmarked against a BCD-SCA approach.
result: Numerical results show the proposed metaheuristic methods improve covert energy efficiency while satisfying the covertness constraints compared to the benchmark.
conclusion: Metaheuristic optimization of UAV trajectory and power provides an effective means of achieving energy-efficient covert wireless transmission under uncertainty in warden positions.

title: Generic Linear Momentum Escape For Twist Maps

abstract: ArXiv:2611.00254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that linear momentum escape is generic in the [MATH] topology for smooth potential perturbations of exact symplectic twist maps, for every [MATH]. method: It uses generating functions, uniform twist conditions, and smooth potential perturbations to establish open dense sets of potentials realizing small momentum drifts.
result: For every sufficiently small momentum drift, an orbit realizes it for an open dense set of potentials, while counterexamples show the result does not generally extend to the C^1 topology.
conclusion: The paper provides a mathematical genericity theorem in symplectic dynamics with examples delimiting its scope, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Variance-reduced First-order Methods For Finite-sum Function Constrained Convex Optimization
authors: Digvijay Boob Yasin Gharehmohammadlou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies finite-sum convex optimization with convex function constraints, where both the objective [MATH] and the constraint mapping [MATH] may have a large number of components. title: A Hierarchical Direct Solver For Lippmann-Schwinger Equations Based On Boundary Traces
authors: Yunhui Cai, Simon Dirckx, Joar Bagge, Per-Gunnar Martinsson
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A high-order hierarchical direct solver for variable-media scattering in two dimensions is presented. Standard discretizations for these problems produce dense linear systems that are commonly solved iteratively, requiring a new global solve for each incident field. The method proposed here instead constructs a reusable scattering operator for the inhomogeneous medium, based on a hierarchical subdivision of the computational domain. First, high-accuracy leaf scattering operators are built from discretized local integral equations. Up the hierarchy, neighboring boxes are merged to build the scattering operators for successively larger boxes. A key feature of the method is that each scattering operator is represented as a map of incoming traces to outgoing traces. Consequently, volume unknowns appear only in the leaf computations; all higher levels of the hierarchy operate entirely on boundary traces. The hierarchical solver is presented first at the continuum level and discretized only afterward using high-order local volume quadrature, polynomial trace representations, and boundary integral techniques. For a discretization involving [MATH] degrees of freedom, the method requires [MATH] work and [MATH] storage to build all scattering operators. Once these are available, any incoming field can be processed at cost [MATH] if only the outgoing field is required, and cost [MATH] if the full field is required. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy on a range of challenging scattering problems including cavities, back-scattering, limited regularity, and high wavenumber, that pose significant challenges to iterative methods.

motivation: Standard discretizations of variable-media scattering yield dense linear systems requiring repeated global solves for each incident field, so the authors aim to build a reusable scattering operator for the medium.
method: The domain is hierarchically subdivided; leaf scattering operators are computed from local integral equations, and larger-box operators are built by merging neighboring boxes, with higher levels represented as maps from incoming to outgoing boundary traces.

conclusion: The hierarchical boundary-trace approach provides an efficient direct solver for variable-media scattering, though it is a numerical/computational physics contribution rather than one aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Completing The Classification Of Hopf Superalgebras Of Dimension Up To 10
authors: Taiki Shibata (okayama University Of Science), Kenichi Shimizu (shibaura Institute Of Technology), Ryota Wakao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a family of semisimple Hopf superalgebras obtained from abelian extensions. Using this family and bosonization, we complete the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We also determine the duals of the semisimple classes with nonzero odd part and give tables of the complete classification.
tldr: The paper completes the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero by introducing a new family from abelian extensions and bosonization.
motivation: Hopf superalgebras are central algebraic structures behind symmetries of fermionic systems, and a full low-dimensional classification provides a reference catalogue for further structural study.
method: The authors construct a family of semisimple Hopf superalgebras via abelian extensions, apply bosonization to relate them to ordinary Hopf algebras, and enumerate all possibilities up to dimension 10.
result: A complete list of Hopf superalgebras of dimension ≤ 10 is obtained, together with tables of the classification and the duals of semisimple classes with nonzero odd part.
conclusion: The classification settles the low-dimensional landscape of Hopf superalgebras and supplies explicit tables useful for future algebraic and representation-theoretic work.

title: Parameter Bounds And Inverse Approximation For Linearized ReLU$^k$ Networks On The Sphere
authors: Yuqing Liu, Tong Mao, Jonathan W. Siegel, Jinchao Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study direct and inverse approximation for linearized shallow ReLU[MATH] networks on [MATH] with quasi-uniform hidden parameters. For [MATH], under the coefficient growth condition [MATH], we prove that approximation at the order [MATH] is equivalent to membership in the parity-compatible Besov space [MATH]. Mere convergence under the same coefficient budget does not imply this regularity. For unconstrained approximation along a nested parameter sequence, a single ridge function gives a counterexample when [MATH], whereas for [MATH] the endpoint Besov inverse conclusion follows from a Bernstein inequality under antipodal quasi-uniformity. motivation: The authors aim to characterize when approximation by linearized ReLU^k networks is equivalent to belonging to a suitable Besov-type smoothness space.
method: They prove direct and inverse approximation theorems under coefficient growth conditions and use counterexamples and Bernstein inequalities for unconstrained approximation along nested or quasi-uniform parameter sequences.

title: The Statistical Geometry Of Latent Recovery In Hidden Markov Models
authors: Trang Pham, Dung Le, Alessandro Rinaldo, Nhat Ho
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) offer an important capability to interpret fitted latent states and transitions. When emission distributions nearly coincide, a small observation-density error does not ensure accurate estimation of the latent quantities needed for interpretation. This motivates us to characterize convergence rates for latent recovery that account for emission separation. Our main contribution lies in deriving deterministic inverse inequalities that convert Hellinger error between fitted and true densities into bounds on latent recovery errors. We develop these bounds for multivariate Gaussian HMMs with a common, known emission covariance matrix and combine them with a Hellinger estimation guarantee for the global maximum likelihood estimator to obtain latent recovery rates. Although the joint observation distribution is a Gaussian mixture with exponentially many path components, they share the same emission centers across time. Leveraging this shared structure, we show that the separation exponents are governed by the maximum number of simultaneously approaching centers rather than the number of path components. Under exact specification, the global bounds on state-sequence probability discrepancies and the 1-Wasserstein loss for latent location distributions exhibit sharp separation exponents that do not increase with the number of selected times. Moreover, sufficiently small observation-density error guarantees unique matching between fitted and true emission centers, which yields error bounds for individual emission centers and transition rows. Under over-specification, individual split-state transition rows are not necessarily identifiable, so we quantify aggregate latent recovery errors and show that state-sequence probability bounds incur larger separation exponents compared to exact specification. We conduct synthetic experiments to validate our theoretical results.
tldr: The paper derives deterministic inverse inequalities converting Hellinger error between fitted and true emission densities into convergence rates for latent-state recovery in multivariate Gaussian hidden Markov models, with separation exponents governed by the maximum number of simultaneously approaching emission centers.
motivation: In HMMs, when emission distributions nearly coincide, small observation-density error does not guarantee accurate recovery of latent quantities, so interpretation-oriented guarantees must explicitly account for emission separation.
method: The authors prove inverse (anti-concentration) inequalities bounding latent recovery error by Hellinger distance for Gaussian HMMs with known common covariance, then combine these with Hellinger rates for the global MLE, exploiting the shared emission-center structure across time.
result: They obtain state-sequence probability bounds and 1-Wasserstein bounds on latent location distributions with sharp separation exponents independent of the number of time points under exact specification, plus identifiability and per-center/transition-row error bounds for small density error; under over-specification only aggregate errors are identifiable and exponents are larger.
conclusion: The results give a statistical-geometric characterization of when and how fast latent HMM structure can be recovered, validated by synthetic experiments.

title: Flux Vector Splittings And Semi-implicit Finite Volume Schemes For An Isentropic Two-phase Flow Model
authors: Michael Dumbser, Gabriella Puppo, Alessandra Spilimbergo, Tommaso Tenna
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present two new semi-implicit finite volume schemes for the 1D hyperbolic and thermodynamically compatible (HTC) isentropic two-phase flow model of Romenski et al., written in terms of mixture density, volume fraction, partial gas density, mixture momentum and the relative phase velocity. In gas-liquid mixtures, the sound speed of the weakly compressible liquid is much larger than the gas sound speed and flow velocity, so the time step of fully explicit discretizations is dictated by liquid acoustic waves, even when the interest lies in the dynamics of the gas. To overcome this difficulty, the model's flux is split at the continuous level into an explicit subsystem (gas dynamics) and an implicit subsystem (liquid acoustic waves), leading to a nonlinear system for liquid pressure solved with the Newton method. In the first splitting the entire liquid phase is treated implicitly, while in the second the liquid convective terms are moved to the explicit subsystem, so only liquid acoustic waves are treated implicitly and nested Picard iterations are avoided. Thus, the time step of both schemes is restricted only by flow velocities and gas sound speed, independent of liquid sound speed. We prove and numerically confirm that both schemes exactly preserve the Abgrall condition (uniform velocity and pressure across material interfaces). For well-prepared initial data, both schemes are consistent with the volume balance of the liquid's low Mach number limit. Riemann problems, pressure equilibrium tests and acoustic tests show that in non-stiff regimes the semi-implicit schemes reproduce the results of a fully explicit scheme, while in the stiff regime they allow time steps that are up to 3-4 orders of magnitude larger, avoiding the excessive numerical dissipation of explicit schemes whose numerical viscosity is dictated by liquid sound speed.
tldr: The paper introduces semi-implicit finite volume schemes for a 1D isentropic two-phase flow model using flux vector splitting to avoid liquid-sound-speed time-step restrictions.
motivation: In gas-liquid mixtures, the liquid sound speed is much larger than the gas sound speed, so fully explicit schemes are severely limited by stiff liquid acoustic waves even when gas dynamics are of interest.
method: The flux is split at the continuous level into an explicit gas-dynamics subsystem and an implicit liquid-acoustic subsystem; two splittings are proposed, one treating the entire liquid phase implicitly and another treating only liquid acoustic waves implicitly, with Newton or nested Picard iterations as needed.
result: Both schemes exactly preserve the Abgrall condition, are consistent with the liquid low-Mach volume balance for well-prepared data, match fully explicit results in non-stiff regimes, and allow 3-4 orders of magnitude larger time steps in stiff regimes.
conclusion: The semi-implicit flux-splitting approach efficiently handles stiff two-phase flow while avoiding excessive numerical dissipation from explicit schemes.

title: Towards An Operational Proof-theoretic Semantics
authors: Alexander V. Gheorghiu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model-theoretic semantics comes with a computational counterpart: to check validity is to search for a countermodel, and tableaux, resolution, and satisfiability solvers make the semantics something one can run. Proof-theoretic semantics -- the younger paradigm in which meaning is given by inferential role rather than by denotation -- has no established counterpart. This paper proposes one: logic programming. We show that Sandqvist's base-extension semantics for intuitionistic propositional logic is executable in a precise sense. Bases are logic programs, and to each formula [MATH] we assign a goal [MATH] of a second-order hereditary Harrop language such that [MATH] is supported in a base [MATH] exactly when [MATH] is operationally derivable from [MATH] read as a program. The encoding is the Russell-Prawitz translation of the connectives with quantification restricted to atoms, and this restriction is not a limitation but the point: it is what the support clauses themselves demand. The correspondence is exact base by base, not merely at the level of validity, so that intuitionistic validity becomes the success of a single query against the empty program. Logic programming stands to proof-theoretic semantics as tableaux and satisfiability solvers stand to model-theoretic semantics.
tldr: The paper gives an operational, executable counterpart to proof-theoretic semantics by encoding Sandqvist's base-extension semantics for intuitionistic propositional logic into second-order hereditary Harrop logic programming.
motivation: Model-theoretic semantics has computational counterparts (tableaux, resolution, SAT solvers), but proof-theoretic semantics lacks an established executable analogue; this work proposes logic programming to fill that gap.
method: Bases are read as logic programs and each formula is assigned a goal in a second-order hereditary Harrop language via a Russell-Prawitz translation of connectives with quantification restricted to atoms, giving an exact base-by-base correspondence.
result: Support of a formula in a base holds exactly when the corresponding goal is operationally derivable from the program, so intuitionistic validity reduces to success of a single query against the empty program.
conclusion: Logic programming stands to proof-theoretic semantics as tableaux and satisfiability solvers stand to model-theoretic semantics, providing a precise operational account of inferential-role meaning.

title: The Complexity Of Choosing Parity Projections
authors: Nicholas Smirnov Karthik Sheshadri

Without a bound on cube size, both problems are [MATH]-complete and NP-hard to approximate within [MATH] for every fixed [MATH]. Our hardness proofs use a crown construction that embeds maximal monomials of parity-projected circuits into positive 2CNF. This yields completeness and inapproximability results, as well as a dichotomy for Boolean constraint languages of arity at most two: the bounded constant derivative problem is in P when all relations are affine and [MATH]-complete otherwise. We also give algorithms parameterized by the number of quadratic rounds, treewidth, or ordered branching-program width, with lower bounds for the first two unless [MATH]. The treewidth lower bound holds for circuits; the case of 2CNF remains open.
tldr: The paper analyzes the parameterized complexity of finding small cubes (parity projections) with constant derivative in Boolean circuits, establishing completeness, inapproximability, and dichotomy results for the associated decision problems.
motivation: Cube attacks in cryptanalysis rely on finding small sets of variables whose parity sum is constant, and the authors aim to characterize the computational hardness of these bounded constant derivative problems.
method: They introduce a crown construction embedding maximal monomials of parity-projected circuits into positive 2CNF, and combine parameterized complexity arguments with algorithms parameterized by quadratic rounds, treewidth, and ordered branching-program width.
result: The sum-1 problem is fixed-parameter tractable in cube size while the sum-0 analogue is not (unless FPT=W[1]); without a cube-size bound both are NP-complete and hard to approximate, and a dichotomy holds for Boolean constraint languages of arity at most two.
conclusion: The work delineates sharp complexity separations for parity-projection problems in cryptanalysis, leaving the 2CNF treewidth case open.

title: Information Design For Behaviorally Stable Platooning
authors: Di Chen Jia Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Voluntary platoon formation requires vehicles to coordinate despite uncertain downstream fuel savings and private joining incentives. We study whether an informed operator can encourage participation by designing a public disclosure rule. A finite-vehicle coordination game links physical fuel savings to vehicles' joining decisions under two information environments: private joining costs and private observations of the common corridor state. Private costs yield a posterior-mean participation response, while private observations require richer posterior information and create correlated formation outcomes. We formulate persuasive disclosure problems and develop computational methods for both regimes. In a literature-anchored reference scenario, optimized two-message disclosure supports participation of 8.74% and 51.83%, respectively, compared with zero without disclosure and 5.15% and 39.27% under full disclosure. Gains concentrate in intermediate opportunities, depend on joining-cost calibration, and need not maximize welfare. Numerical sensitivity and trajectory checks quantify these effects. All gains are conditional on favorable symmetric equilibrium selection: public information alone cannot eliminate the no-participation equilibrium when joining requires a costly commitment without a guaranteed partner.
tldr: The paper studies optimal public information disclosure (Bayesian persuasion) by an operator to encourage voluntary vehicle platoon formation in a finite-vehicle coordination game.
motivation: Voluntary platooning requires coordination under uncertain fuel savings and private joining incentives, so an informed operator may benefit from designing what information to reveal to vehicles.
method: A finite-vehicle coordination game is formulated under two information environments (private joining costs vs. private observations of the corridor state), yielding persuasive disclosure optimization problems solved with computational methods, plus numerical sensitivity and trajectory checks in a literature-anchored scenario.
result: Optimized two-message disclosure raises participation to 8.74% and 51.83% in the two regimes (vs. 0% with no disclosure and 5.15%/39.27% under full disclosure), with gains concentrated at intermediate opportunities and not necessarily welfare-maximizing.
conclusion: Strategic information design can improve platooning participation, but public information alone cannot eliminate the no-participation equilibrium when joining is a costly commitment without a guaranteed partner.

title: A Density Theorem For Non-standard Irreducible Cyclic Codes
authors: Tao Feng, Henk D. L. Hollmann, Weicong Li, Qing Xiang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a fixed-characteristic density form of the Berger-Charpin conjecture for non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes: for each prime [MATH], the lengths admitting such a non-standard code over some finite field of characteristic [MATH] have natural density zero. Thus, for almost every length coprime to [MATH], every such code over every finite field of characteristic [MATH] has only the permutation automorphisms generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius map. The proof uses the Feng--Hollmann--Li--Xiang classification for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes, a normal form for the deriving constructions in that paper, and a theorem by Wiertelak on multiplicative orders, in the form recalled by Moree.
tldr: The paper proves a density-zero result for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes over finite fields of fixed characteristic, supporting a density form of the Berger-Charpin conjecture.
motivation: Irreducible cyclic codes are a classical coding-theory family, and the Berger-Charpin conjecture concerns their permutation automorphisms; the authors aim to show that non-standard examples are rare as the code length varies.
method: The proof combines the Feng-Hollmann-Li-Xiang classification of non-standard irreducible cyclic codes, a normal form for the deriving constructions, and Wiertelak's theorem on multiplicative orders as recalled by Moree.
result: For each prime characteristic, the set of lengths admitting a non-degenerate non-standard irreducible cyclic code over some finite field of that characteristic has natural density zero.
conclusion: Almost every length coprime to the characteristic yields only the permutation automorphisms generated by the cyclic shift and Frobenius map, confirming the conjectured rarity of non-standard cases.

title: E-ude: A Scientific Machine Learning Model For Malware Propagation Dynamics
authors: Vineet Kumar, Samiran Ghosh, V Anil Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the malware propagation dynamics over the Internet is crucial for effectively controlling its spread. Existing mechanistic and data-driven models in the context of malware propagation dynamics, have some issues with either interpretability or predictive accuracy. This study presents an Enhanced Universal Differential Equation (E-UDE) framework that explicitly incorporates more detailed key factors that influence malware propagation. Evaluation on real-world malware propagation data shows that the E-UDE achieves the best overall performance, attaining an overall RMSE of 783.70 and MAE of 421.65. Compared with the Classical ODE and the UDE models, the proposed approach reduces RMSE by approximately 66 percent and 39 percent, respectively. Its robustness to predictive capability is further evaluated. In this experiment, the E-UDE achieves a Test RMSE of 634.6, a Test MAE of 419.3, and a Test Correlation of 0.964. The E-UDE maintains relatively stable prediction performance as the noise level increases, showing limited degradation compared with the baseline models. Furthermore, this E-UDE model enables us to perform several scenario analyses under different cybersecurity scenarios, providing a useful framework for better understanding the effective control factors. To study the wide applicability of the E-UDE framework, the model performance is assessed by two different datasets, namely, Code Red dataset and Witty Worm dataset.
tldr: The paper proposes an Enhanced Universal Differential Equation (E-UDE) framework, a scientific machine learning model for predicting malware propagation dynamics over the Internet.
motivation: Existing mechanistic and data-driven models of malware spread either lack interpretability or predictive accuracy, motivating a hybrid approach that incorporates more detailed key factors.
method: The authors combine mechanistic ordinary differential equations with learned neural components in an Enhanced UDE framework, trained and evaluated on real-world malware propagation datasets (Code Red and Witty Worm).
result: E-UDE achieves an overall RMSE of 783.70 and MAE of 421.65, reducing RMSE by ~66% and ~39% versus Classical ODE and UDE baselines, with a Test RMSE of 634.6 and correlation of 0.964, while remaining robust to noise.
conclusion: The E-UDE framework provides accurate, interpretable, and robust malware propagation forecasting and supports scenario analyses for cybersecurity control factors.

title: The Blind Spots Of Detection: Adversarial Perturbation Attacks Against Watchdogs In Distributed Llm Inference
authors: Siu Wai Shi, Xiaochen Zhu, Xinjian Luo, Keke Huang, Bingxue Zhang, Xiaofeng Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.01097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decentralizing large language model (LLM) inference across untrusted Web nodes requires robust verification to ensure computational integrity. Existing activation-based verification and detection mechanisms validate intermediate outputs against reference values, permitting bounded numerical deviations to accommodate benign cross-hardware discrepancies. However, a critical security question remains: what can a malicious worker achieve while operating within these tolerance bounds? In this work, we introduce Hush-Up, a stealthy availability attack against distributed LLM inference, where a single malicious worker halts generation while evading attribution. The attacker first profiles its local execution to model an empirical bound of benign hardware errors. Using this error bound as a feasibility constraint, the attacker optimizes an adversarial perturbation on its output activations to maximize the final-layer probability of the end-of-sequence (EOS) token, i.e., to hush up the model. Across diverse models and benchmarks, Hush-Up effectively forces premature generation termination and collapses model capabilities. Furthermore, the attack hushes up the watchdogs themselves: existing defenses often fail to detect the sabotage entirely or falsely attribute the amplified downstream anomalies to honest workers. Our findings expose a fundamental gap between local numerical verification and end-to-end accountability: perturbations too small to indict a worker locally can nevertheless be powerful enough to break distributed inference globally.
tldr: The paper introduces Hush-Up, a stealthy availability attack that manipulates activation perturbations within benign hardware-error tolerances to force premature EOS generation in distributed LLM inference while evading watchdog attribution.
motivation: Decentralized LLM inference across untrusted nodes requires robust verification, but existing activation-based watchdogs allow bounded numerical deviations. The authors ask what a malicious worker can achieve within those tolerance bounds.
method: The attacker profiles local execution to estimate benign hardware-error bounds, then optimizes an adversarial activation perturbation constrained by those bounds to maximize the final-layer EOS token probability.
result: Across models and benchmarks, Hush-Up forces premature generation termination, collapses model capabilities, and often evades detection or falsely attributes downstream anomalies to honest workers.
conclusion: The work exposes a fundamental gap between local numerical verification and end-to-end accountability in distributed LLM inference.

title: Exploring Collaborative Debating Models For The Future Of Science
authors: Zeki C. Seskir
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI is expanding what researchers can produce. A substantial increase in scientific output would also change how that work is organised and distributed, as earlier shifts in the scale of science have done. This paper develops a thought experiment around Collaborative Debating Models (CDMs), topic-focused environments where researchers work with AI and one another to pursue questions and maintain an evolving account of their field. Individual contributions would remain attributable as ongoing debate and further analysis change the shared account. The paper considers how journals could evolve into these gathering places and how different forms of ownership would shape scientific agendas and the support for continuing work. CDMs could connect participants to remote laboratories and other research services to conduct new studies, with shared repositories making the resulting data available for further inquiry. The proposal links expanded scientific production to collective interpretation through continuing assessment and revision, while leaving room for disciplinary differences in how contributions are reviewed and recognised.
tldr: The paper proposes Collaborative Debating Models (CDMs) as AI-mediated, topic-focused environments for organizing future scientific research and collective interpretation.
motivation: AI is increasing scientific output, which may require new ways to organize, attribute, review, and distribute research similar to earlier scale shifts in science.
method: The author develops a thought experiment describing CDMs where researchers collaborate with AI and each other, potentially transforming journals into gathering places and linking participants to remote laboratories and shared data repositories.
result: The proposal outlines how CDMs could connect expanded scientific production with ongoing debate, attribution, ownership structures, and disciplinary differences in review and recognition.
conclusion: CDMs are presented as a speculative organizational model for future science, but the paper does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spectral Fields And Unitary Descent: Local Splitting, Simultaneous Norms, And Transcendental Obstructions
authors: Angel Cano, Nikolay Gusevskii, Marlon M. L\'opez-Flores
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral fields can recover matrix coefficients without standardizing the invariant Hermitian form. Over an algebraic subfield of [MATH] stable under nontrivial complex conjugation, we prove that every Zariski-dense subgroup in a normalized Hermitian model of dimension [MATH] and signature [MATH] at the fixed embedding contains a loxodromic element whose spectrum makes all diagonal coefficients norms. The element can be chosen so that every positive power is regular and generates the same splitting field. For an arbitrary initial Hermitian model over such a field, two spectra suffice for standard unitary descent over an extension of relative degree at most [MATH]. Over every quadratic extension [MATH] of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic zero, a four-dimensional quasi-split unitary group of Witt index two contains a discrete, Zariski-dense free subgroup whose spectra all split over [MATH]. Over intrinsic fields of positive transcendence degree, we construct a single convex cocompact, Zariski-dense free subgroup of [MATH] for which, for every initial regular element and every normalized extraction, the Hermitian obstruction persists after adjoining any finite family of spectra and over the total spectral field.
tldr: This paper studies spectral fields, unitary descent, and Hermitian obstructions for Zariski-dense subgroups and quasi-split unitary groups over local and transcendental fields.
motivation: The work aims to recover matrix coefficients without standardizing invariant Hermitian forms and to understand when spectra suffice for unitary descent in Hermitian models.
method: It uses algebraic and number-theoretic constructions involving Zariski-dense subgroups, loxodromic elements, splitting fields, quadratic extensions of nonarchimedean local fields, and convex cocompact free subgroups.
result: The authors prove existence of loxodromic elements whose spectra make diagonal coefficients norms, show two spectra suffice for unitary descent over bounded-degree extensions, and construct subgroups with persistent Hermitian obstructions.
conclusion: The paper contributes to pure mathematics, specifically unitary group theory and spectral field obstructions, with no apparent connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On The Complexity Of Isomorphism Problems For Tensors, Groups, And Polynomials V: Over Commutative Rings
authors: Joshua A. Grochow, Youming Qiao, Katherine E. Stange, Xiaorui Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensors over commutative rings naturally appear in number theory, geometry, and group theory. For example, [MATH] tensors over [MATH] form the starting point of Bhargava's celebrated works generalising Gauss's composition law (Bhargava, Ann. Math., 2004). Symmetric tensors over [MATH] are central to the classification of Calabi--Yau threefolds (Yau, Commun. Pure Appl. Math., 1978; Wall, Invent. Math., 1966), geometric objects of significance in string theory. Additionally, tensors over finite commutative rings closely correspond to finite nilpotent groups of class 2 (Baer, Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 1938). In this work, we study isomorphism testing of tensors over commutative rings from a complexity-theoretic viewpoint, and its applications. Some of our main results are: 1. Let [MATH] be a commutative ring. We introduce two complexity classes: [MATH] consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three modules over [MATH], and [MATH] consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three free modules over [MATH]. 2. We show that some classical problems considered by Grunewald and Segal (ibid.), and the problem of classifying Calabi--Yau threefolds, are [MATH]-complete. We also show that many natural problems are complete for [MATH]. 3. We show that testing isomorphism of tensors in [MATH] is polynomial-time equivalent to the principal ideal problem in algorithmic number theory. 4. We present an [MATH]-time algorithm for testing isomorphism of finite nilpotent groups of class [MATH] and odd order [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of isomorphism problems for tensors, groups, and polynomials over commutative rings, with no apparent quantum-information content.
motivation: Tensors over commutative rings arise in number theory, geometry, and group theory, motivating a complexity-theoretic classification of their isomorphism problems and related algebraic classification tasks.
method: The authors introduce complexity classes based on polynomial-time reductions to isomorphism of tensor products of modules and free modules over commutative rings, and prove completeness results and algorithms within this framework.
result: They show that several classical classification problems, including Calabi-Yau threefold classification, are complete for the new classes; relate tensor isomorphism to the principal ideal problem; and give an algorithm for finite nilpotent groups of class 2 and odd order.
conclusion: The work advances algebraic and complexity-theoretic understanding of tensor isomorphism over commutative rings, but it does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stability Of Solitons In The Parametrically Driven And Damped Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation In Arbitrary Dimension
authors: Fernando Carre\~no-Navas
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spectral stability of soliton solutions of the parametrically driven and damped nonlinear Schr\"odinger (PDDNLS) equation with power-law nonlinearity [MATH] in [MATH] dimensions. We identify two families of stationary solutions, [MATH], whose existence is determined by two conditions: one involving the nonlinearity exponent~[MATH] and the spatial dimension~[MATH], and another involving the forcing amplitude~[MATH] and the damping coefficient~[MATH]. By linearising around these solutions and introducing a convenient parametrisation through~[MATH], we reduce the stability problem to a dissipationless eigenvalue problem for two Schr\"odinger-type operators, [MATH] and [MATH]. We prove that [MATH] is always unstable, while for [MATH], we carry out a complete spectral analysis by decomposing the problem into angular momentum sectors [MATH]. We show that modes with [MATH] generate no instabilities and that no complex quadruplets arise on~[MATH]. We also derive an analytical instability criterion on [MATH] by combining a Vakhitov--Kolokolov-type argument with a local analysis that determines the direction of the eigenvalue splitting near the origin. In addition, we uncover new phenomena at both small and large values of [MATH] that were not investigated in earlier one-dimensional studies. Numerical stability diagrams for [MATH] are presented.
tldr: A spectral stability analysis of soliton solutions to the parametrically driven, damped nonlinear Schrodinger equation with power-law nonlinearity in arbitrary spatial dimension.
motivation: Solitons in driven-dissipative nonlinear Schrodinger models are relevant to pattern formation and nonlinear wave physics, and earlier stability results were limited largely to one dimension; the author aims to generalize to arbitrary dimension and arbitrary power-law exponent.
method: Two families of stationary solutions are identified and linearized about; a parametrization reduces the linear stability problem to a dissipationless eigenvalue problem for two Schrodinger-type operators, analyzed by angular-momentum sector decomposition, a Vakhitov-Kolokolov-type argument, and local eigenvalue-splitting analysis.
result: One solution family is proven always unstable, while for the second family modes with nonzero angular momentum generate no instabilities and no complex eigenvalue quadruplets appear; an analytical instability criterion is derived and numerical stability diagrams are given.
conclusion: The work extends one-dimensional stability theory of parametrically driven damped NLS solitons to arbitrary dimension and reveals new small- and large-parameter phenomena, though it remains a purely classical nonlinear-PDE study.

title: Comments On "Multidimensional Costas Arrays And Their Periodicity"
authors: Shiv Munagala
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rubio and Torres conjectured that a multidimensional Costas array, defined by a bijection between two boxes of integer points whose domain has at least as many dimensions as its image, can stay Costas in every window of its periodic extension only if its order is a power of two fixed by the dimension of the domain. We give a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order [MATH], with a two-dimensional domain and a two-dimensional image, so the conjecture is false. The verification reduces to [MATH] windows. It has been confirmed by computer and in the Lean proof assistant. The array also meets with equality the pigeonhole bound that Rubio and Torres use for their non-existence results, so that bound is tight.
tldr: The paper refutes a conjecture by Rubio and Torres on multidimensional Costas arrays by constructing a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order 2^something with a two-dimensional domain and image, verified by computer and in Lean.
motivation: Rubio and Torres conjectured that multidimensional Costas arrays that remain Costas in every window of their periodic extension must have order a power of two determined by the domain dimension; the author aims to test this conjecture.
method: Explicit construction of a 4D periodic Costas array with 2D domain and 2D image, with verification reduced to a finite number of windows (checked by computer and formalized in the Lean proof assistant).
result: The conjecture is false: the constructed array is periodic-Costas, and it meets with equality the pigeonhole bound used by Rubio and Torres, showing that bound is tight.
conclusion: Multidimensional periodic Costas arrays exist beyond the conjectured power-of-two order restriction, and formal verification supports the counterexample.

title: Costate Estimation And Covector Mapping For Bernstein Polynomial Direct Methods In Optimal Control
authors: Venanzio Cichella, Isaac Kaminer, Claire Walton, Naira Hovakimyan, Antonio Pascoal
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bernstein polynomial approximation of continuous functions has a slower rate of convergence as compared to other approximation methods. ``The fact seems to have precluded any numerical application of Bernstein polynomials from having been made. Perhaps they will find application when the properties of the approximant in the large are of more importance than the closeness of the approximation.'' -- has remarked P.J. Davis in his 1963 book Interpolation and Approximation. This paper presents a direct approximation method for nonlinear optimal control problems with mixed input and state constraints based on Bernstein polynomial approximation, in which the dynamic and path constraints are imposed at the Bernstein coefficients (control points). We provide a rigorous analysis showing that, under convergence assumptions on the control polygons, the proposed method yields consistent approximations of time continuous optimal control problems and can be used for costate estimation of the optimal control problems. In particular, multipliers satisfying a relaxed Karush Kuhn Tucker system of the resulting nonlinear program, scaled by the quadrature weight, approximate the costate and the multipliers of the optimal control problem. Owing to the structure of the Bernstein differentiation matrix, the discrete transversality conditions are contained in the relaxed Karush Kuhn Tucker system, and no additional closure conditions need to be added to it. This result leads to the formulation of the Covector Mapping Theorem for Bernstein polynomial approximation.
tldr: The paper develops a Bernstein-polynomial-based direct method for nonlinear optimal control with mixed state/input constraints and proves a Covector Mapping Theorem linking NLP multipliers to costates.
motivation: Bernstein polynomial approximations converge slowly, which historically discouraged their use, but their control-point structure makes constraint imposition and costate recovery convenient for direct optimal control.
method: Dynamic and path constraints are imposed at Bernstein coefficients (control points); a relaxed Karush-Kuhn-Tucker system of the discretized nonlinear program, scaled by quadrature weights, is analyzed to approximate costates and multipliers.
result: Under convergence assumptions on the control polygons, the method gives consistent approximations of the continuous optimal control problem, and the discrete transversality conditions emerge automatically from the Bernstein differentiation matrix without extra closure conditions.
conclusion: The authors establish a Covector Mapping Theorem for Bernstein polynomial approximation, enabling reliable costate estimation in direct optimal control.

title: Constraint Qualifications And Regularity Conditions For Nonlinear Constraint Systems
authors: Shiji Zuo, Qihang Lin, Wei Liu, Yangyang Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constraint qualifications (CQs) and regularity conditions (RCs) play a fundamental role in establishing global iteration and oracle complexity results for first-order methods on solving functional constrained optimization problems. Various conditions have been proposed and employed in the literature, with their validity established for different classes of applications. However, the use of different conditions across existing studies makes it difficult to directly compare their theoretical results and underlying assumptions. In this report, we systematically review several widely used CQs and RCs and investigate their relationships. In particular, we establish implications among these conditions and identify cases in which the implications are strict, thereby clarifying their relative strengths. Our results provide a unified perspective on existing regularity assumptions and offer guidance for selecting appropriate conditions in the complexity analysis of first-order methods.
tldr: A systematic review of constraint qualifications and regularity conditions used in the complexity analysis of first-order methods for functional constrained optimization.
motivation: Existing studies on functional constrained optimization employ different constraint qualifications and regularity conditions, which hinders direct comparison of theoretical results and assumptions.
method: The authors survey several widely used constraint qualifications and regularity conditions, establish implications among them, and identify cases where these implications are strict.
result: A unified hierarchy of regularity assumptions is derived, clarifying the relative strength of the various conditions and showing where strict separations hold.
conclusion: The report offers guidance for selecting appropriate conditions in complexity analyses of first-order methods for constrained optimization.

title: Maximum Principle For Discrete-time Stochastic Recursive Games Driven By Fractional Noises
authors: Yuecai Han, Yuhang Li, Chenfei Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates discrete-time stochastic recursive games driven by fractional noises, in which the cost functional is defined through a backward stochastic difference equation. By introducing discrete-time adjoint equations, we establish a maximum principle and the verification theorem for open-loop Nash equilibria in non-zero sum and zero sum stochastic recursive game problems. The effectiveness of our theorem is demonstrated through applications to two different linear-quadratic stochastic recursive games and a portfolio selection problem with a recursive utility functional.
tldr: The paper derives a maximum principle and verification theorem for discrete-time stochastic recursive games driven by fractional noises.
motivation: It aims to characterize open-loop Nash equilibria in non-zero-sum and zero-sum stochastic recursive games where the cost is defined via backward stochastic difference equations.
method: The authors introduce discrete-time adjoint equations and use them to establish a stochastic maximum principle and verification theorem, with applications to linear-quadratic games and a portfolio selection problem.
