result: The proposed maximum principle yields equilibrium conditions and is illustrated through two linear-quadratic recursive game examples and a recursive-utility portfolio problem.
conclusion: The work extends stochastic recursive game theory to fractional-noise discrete-time settings and provides verifiable equilibrium conditions for applied problems.

title: Agent4FreeFem: A Verification-Guided Framework For Autonomous Topology Optimization
authors: Zhipu Cui, Helin Gong, Shengfeng Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topology optimization has become an indispensable design tool in the aerospace, automotive, and mechanical engineering industries. Yet bringing a new problem from its description to an optimized result remains slow, expert-dependent, and unreliable: the workflow spans many manually connected stages, each new problem requires solver code to be written and debugged manually, and such code often fails or yields incorrect results. We present Agent4FreeFem, a pipeline driven by a large language model that turns a natural-language problem description into a set of verified optimization results without manual solver-code development or debugging. The pipeline keeps the problem definition unmodified, localizes errors using independent sources of evidence, and completes constrained repairs automatically, thereby providing efficient end-to-end automation, autonomous execution, and verifiable results. We evaluated Agent4FreeFem on a suite of single-physics and coupled multiphysics problems. Every case passed runtime verification and finished within the repair budget of each stage.
tldr: Agent4FreeFem is an LLM-driven pipeline that automates topology optimization from natural-language problem descriptions to verified FreeFem solver results.
motivation: Topology optimization workflows are slow, expert-dependent, and error-prone because solver code must be manually written, debugged, and validated for each new problem.
method: The framework uses a large language model to generate and repair FreeFem solver code, guided by independent verification evidence and constrained automated repair while keeping the problem definition unchanged.
result: Evaluated on single-physics and coupled multiphysics problems, every case passed runtime verification and completed within the repair budget of each stage.
conclusion: The work demonstrates end-to-end autonomous topology optimization with verifiable results, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Semi-parametric Bernstein-von Mises Theorem At Rate $n^{-3/2}$ For Frequency Estimation
authors: Paulo Serra
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Bayesian inference for the frequency of a periodic signal of unknown shape, observed in Gaussian white noise on the interval [MATH]. The information about the frequency grows like [MATH], so the frequency can be estimated at rate [MATH], while the shape is an infinite-dimensional nuisance parameter. We endow the frequency and the shape with independent priors, the prior on the shape being a random series in the trigonometric basis. We give conditions on the priors under which the posterior for the signal contracts at a rate that, for suitable choices, is the minimax rate for Sobolev classes of smoothness at least one, up to a logarithmic factor and adaptively to the smoothness of the shape. If, moreover, the prior keeps the shape away from shapes with a shorter period, also the marginal posteriors for the frequency and the shape contract around the truth. Under further conditions, which hold for a Gaussian random series prior conditioned to keep the shape away from shapes with a shorter period, for every true shape with smallest period 1 and Sobolev smoothness larger than [MATH], the marginal posterior for the frequency satisfies a semi-parametric Bernstein-von Mises theorem at rate [MATH], which we prove by moving the origin of time, a change that leaves the posterior unchanged when the prior on the shape is invariant under time shifts.
tldr: A classical Bayesian statistics paper proving a semi-parametric Bernstein-von Mises theorem at rate n^{-3/2} for estimating the frequency of a periodic signal of unknown shape in Gaussian white noise.
motivation: Frequentist and Bayesian inference for periodic signals with unknown shape involves an infinite-dimensional nuisance parameter, and understanding when marginal posteriors for the frequency behave Gaussianly (Bernstein-von Mises) at fast rates is of interest in classical nonparametric statistics.
method: Independent priors are placed on the frequency and on the shape (a random trigonometric series); contraction rates for the posterior are derived under conditions on the priors, and a change-of-time-origin argument exploiting shift invariance is used to prove the semi-parametric Bernstein-von Mises theorem.
result: The posterior contracts at the minimax rate for Sobolev classes (up to a log factor, adaptively in smoothness), marginal posteriors contract around the truth when shapes with shorter periods are excluded, and a semi-parametric Bernstein-von Mises theorem at rate n^{-3/2} holds for the frequency under a Gaussian random series prior.
conclusion: The work delivers asymptotic normality of the marginal posterior for frequency estimation in a semi-parametric periodic-signal model, but it is a purely classical statistical result with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Kerkoporta: Injecting Structured-Output Backdoors In Reasoning Coding Agents
authors: Georgios Syros, Blake Bullwinkel, Alina Oprea, Cristina Nita-Rotaru, Amanda Minnich, Xiaodong Liu, Giorgio Severi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing large language model (LLM) backdoor attacks operate primarily in chat settings, where the risk is bounded by free-form text outputs. AI agents remove that bound by performing actions and executing commands on the user's machine. We introduce structured-output backdoor attacks against reasoning models in agentic coding settings. A trigger placed anywhere in the agent's context causes the model to emit an attacker-chosen tool call, which the harness executes, directly compromising the system's confidentiality, integrity, or availability. We present Kerkoporta, a methodology that constructs high-quality poison samples, injects the backdoor via supervised fine-tuning, and recovers utility loss with lightweight reinforcement learning. We evaluate on modern, heavily post-trained open-weight models across proprietary and open-source harnesses, focusing on coding for its wide adoption and long-horizon task structure. The attack reaches success rates of up to 96.2% and can be configured to generalize across harnesses or bind to a single target. The resulting models can outperform the clean baseline on standard utility benchmarks, giving victims a direct incentive to adopt them. Overall, we demonstrate that LLM backdoors can have critical security impacts in the context of modern coding agents, and we characterize the poisoning methodology required to insert backdoors that are both effective and stealthy in this setting.
tldr: Kerkoporta introduces structured-output backdoor attacks that poison reasoning coding agents so a context trigger induces an attacker-chosen tool call executed by the harness.
motivation: Prior LLM backdoor work targets free-form chat outputs, but agentic systems execute actions, so backdoors there can cause real system compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
method: The authors build high-quality poison samples, inject the backdoor via supervised fine-tuning, and recover degraded utility with lightweight reinforcement learning, evaluating heavily post-trained open-weight models across proprietary and open-source agent harnesses.
result: Attack success rates reach up to 96.2%, can generalize across harnesses or bind to a single target, and the poisoned models can even exceed clean baselines on standard utility benchmarks.
conclusion: LLM backdoors carry critical security impact in modern coding agents, and the paper characterizes a poisoning methodology for effective, stealthy injection.

title: Blazing-Fast Smt-lib Parsing For Rust And Lean
authors: Jan Onderka, Armin Biere, Henrik B\"oving
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: SMT-LIB is a standard input format for Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solvers. However, parsing the format is non-trivial and can become a bottleneck, e.g. when retrieving benchmark metadata or normalising the input for solvers. We introduce blazing-smtlib, a Rust parsing library for SMT-LIB, and BSmtLib, its port to Lean. We outline the library API we designed for composability and extensibility (including non-standard SMT-LIB commands), and discuss our implementation decisions for fast lexing and parsing. We proved that our lexing and parsing with Lean-specific optimisations match our formalised reading of the SMT-LIB syntax. We measured performance on a representative sample from the 2025 SMT-LIB corpus and found that blazing-smtlib is more than 6 times faster on the geometric mean than previous parsing libraries and BSmtLib is faster or comparable to them.
tldr: The authors present blazing-smtlib, a fast Rust library for parsing SMT-LIB inputs, and BSmtLib, its Lean port, with verified lexing/parsing semantics and large speedups over prior parsers.
motivation: Parsing SMT-LIB is non-trivial and often a bottleneck when extracting benchmark metadata or normalising solver inputs, motivating a fast, composable, and formally-grounded parser.
method: They design a composable and extensible library API (supporting non-standard commands), make performance-oriented lexing/parsing implementation choices, formalise the SMT-LIB syntax reading, and prove that their Lean-optimised lexer and parser match this formalisation.
result: On a representative sample of the 2025 SMT-LIB corpus, blazing-smtlib is more than 6x faster on the geometric mean than previous parsing libraries, while BSmtLib is faster than or comparable to them.
conclusion: The work delivers practically fast, verified SMT-LIB parsing infrastructure for Rust and Lean, useful for solver tooling and benchmark processing.

title: Online Fair Division Of Chores With Upgrade Recourse
authors: Nicholas Teh Yichen Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the online fair division of indivisible chores among [MATH] agents under upgrade recourse, where earlier assignments may be revised but each chore previously assigned to an agent must be replaced by a distinct chore that she finds no more costly. We show that a simple adaptation of round robin maintains envy-freeness up to one chore (EF1) together with a [MATH]-approximation of the maximin share (MMS), and that no deterministic algorithm without predictions can do better, even when all agents rank the chores in the same order. This stands in contrast to the allocation of goods, where the optimal MMS factor vanishes as [MATH] grows and cannot be achieved together with EF1. Moreover, knowing only the number of chores modulo a period of length [MATH] (and nothing about the costs) suffices to improve upon this factor at the final configuration, while the same algorithm retains a factor below [MATH] even if this information is wrong. On the other hand, envy-freeness up to any chore (EFX) essentially requires the exact number of chores: uncertainty between two consecutive values already rules out every finite approximation, and even exact knowledge does not allow EFX to be combined with an MMS guarantee better than the trivial factor of [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies online fair division of indivisible chores among agents under an 'upgrade recourse' model where prior assignments can be revised, characterizing achievable envy-freeness and maximin-share approximations.
motivation: Online fair division of chores is far less understood than the goods case, and it is unclear what fairness guarantees (EF1, EFX, MMS) are attainable when assignments may be revisited via upgrade recourse, with or without limited predictions.
method: The authors analyze a simple adaptation of the round-robin algorithm under upgrade recourse, prove tight lower bounds for deterministic prediction-free algorithms, and study how partial information (number of chores modulo a period) affects the achievable MMS factor and EFX.
result: Round robin with upgrade recourse achieves EF1 together with an O(1)-type MMS approximation that is optimal without predictions; knowing the chore count modulo a fixed period improves the MMS factor while remaining robust to incorrect information, whereas EFX essentially requires exact knowledge of the number of chores and precludes any nontrivial MMS guarantee.
conclusion: Chore allocation exhibits qualitatively different behavior from goods allocation, and the results delineate sharp information requirements for combining envy-freeness with MMS approximations in online settings.

title: The Long Con On The Web: Earn-then-Exploit Fraud Attacks Against Coding Agents
authors: Xingling Xu, Zhengwei Jiang, Zheng Zhi, Fangming Dong, Lingjia Guo, Wei Dong, Chunyan Ma, Jun Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents increasingly operate with web access and high privileges, creating a new attack surface where web fraud can directly target autonomous agents. Existing studies mainly focus on malicious links, prompt injection, and interface deception, while content-level web fraud against agents and the amplification of attacks through agent trust remain underexplored. In this paper, we present EtE (Earn-then-Exploit), a web fraud attack framework against coding agents, in which a malicious website first provides multiple rounds of genuinely verifiable assistance to establish trust and then introduces task-related instructions that cross intended operational boundaries. To systematically evaluate its effectiveness, we construct 56 organizational environments (8 task contexts x 7 attack consequences) and evaluate three representative coding agents. EtE achieves an average scene-level attack success rate of 71.4%, including 85.7% on Codex-GPT-5.5, 67.9% on ZCode-GLM-5.3-Flash, and 60.7% on QwenCode-Qwen3.7-Plus, significantly outperforming all injection-based baselines. More importantly, our experiments reveal that coding agents exhibit trust-like behavioral reliance on previously helpful Web sources, and that such accumulated credibility significantly increases their susceptibility to subsequent malicious instructions. Based on this finding, we propose action-authorization separation (AAS), which prevents web content from directly authorizing privileged actions and reduces the attack success rate to 0% while preserving 100% task completion, outperforming all evaluated defense baselines.
tldr: The paper introduces EtE (Earn-then-Exploit), a web-fraud attack framework in which malicious websites first provide genuine verifiable help to coding agents and then escalate to boundary-crossing instructions, achieving a 71.4% average attack success rate across 56 environments and three agents.
motivation: Coding agents increasingly browse the web with high privileges, so content-level web fraud that exploits an agent's trust in previously useful sources is underexplored compared to link-based, prompt-injection, or interface-deception attacks.
method: The authors build 56 organizational test environments (8 task contexts x 7 attack consequences), evaluate three representative coding agents against earned-trust fraud chains and injection baselines, and then propose action-authorization separation (AAS) as a defense that prevents web content from authorizing privileged actions.
result: EtE reaches 71.4% average scene-level attack success (85.7% on Codex-GPT-5.5, 67.9% on ZCode-GLM-5.3-Flash, 60.7% on QwenCode-Qwen3.7-Plus), well above injection baselines; AAS cuts success to 0% while retaining 100% task completion.
conclusion: Agents exhibit trust-like reliance on previously helpful web sources that amplifies susceptibility to later malicious instructions, and separating action from authorization neutralizes this class of attack.

title: Closed-Form Gaussian Mixture Representations Of d-Dimensional Triangulated Domains
authors: Ali Darijani, Benedikt Stratmann, Uwe D. Hanebeck, Ratan Bahadur Thapa, J\"urgen Beyerer, Nehal Afifi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a Gaussian Mixture (GM) representation of a full-dimensional subset of Euclidean space with finite volume from a finite simplicial triangulation in closed form. On each simplex, we replace the uniform probability density function (PDF) with a Gaussian PDF that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence, arriving at the information projection onto the family of Gaussian PDFs. By exploiting affine isomorphisms between simplices, the joint convexity and bijection invariance properties of the KL divergence, identities for Dirichlet PDFs, and a partition-of-unity argument, we establish a dimension-dependent but geometry-independent sharp upper bound on the global KL divergence between the resulting GM PDF and the uniform PDF on the original domain. Numerical examples illustrate the construction and demonstrate its potential in practical applications.
tldr: The paper derives closed-form Gaussian mixture representations of uniformly distributed triangulated domains by minimizing KL divergence on each simplex, with a sharp dimension-dependent bound on the global approximation error.
motivation: Uniform densities over triangulated polytopes are awkward to use in probabilistic filtering and estimation pipelines, which prefer Gaussian mixtures; a principled closed-form conversion is therefore desirable.
method: On each simplex the uniform PDF is replaced by its information projection onto Gaussian PDFs (KL minimizer), and affine isomorphisms between simplices plus Dirichlet-PDF identities and a partition-of-unity argument are used to bound the global KL divergence.
result: A geometry-independent, dimension-dependent sharp upper bound on the KL divergence between the mixture PDF and the uniform PDF is established, illustrated with numerical examples.
conclusion: The construction gives a practical, theoretically justified Gaussian-mixture surrogate for uniform distributions on triangulated domains, with applications in estimation and filtering.

title: Digital Twin-Assisted Fast Beam Alignment For mmWave Mimo Networks
authors: Ashfaq Khokhar Muhammad Kamran Saeed
abstract: ArXiv:2611.01107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication relies on directional beam sweeping for initial access, which incurs substantial latency and signaling overhead as antenna arrays grow large and deployments become denser. Machine-learning-based beam prediction can reduce this overhead, but its effectiveness depends on training data that accurately reflects the deployment environment, a requirement that is difficult to meet in practice. This paper presents a latency-aware beam management architecture that integrates digital-twin-assisted prediction, regionbased localization, weighted ensemble learning, and explainability-driven beam pruning into a unified framework. A digital twin (DT) generates site-specific ray-traced channel knowledge offline, enabling environment-aware beam prediction without exhaustive real-world measurements and supporting both initial access and beam tracking. The proposed ensemble learning scheme combines a base classifier and a specialist classifier through reliability-weighted fusion to improve prediction accuracy and robustness, while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based attribution pruning reduces the beam codebook to a small subset of the most informative beams for beam allocation. To capture the distributional mismatch between the DT and real-world environments: the network was trained on imperfect digital-twin data but evaluated on real-world surrobase data. Results show that the proposed method achieves 96.80% top-1 and 98.36% top-3 beam prediction accuracy, while reducing over-the-air sounding overhead by nearly an order of magnitude relative to exhaustive sweeping, outperforming convolutional and deep neural network baselines from prior work.
tldr: A digital-twin-assisted machine-learning framework for fast mmWave MIMO beam alignment that achieves high beam prediction accuracy while cutting sounding overhead by nearly an order of magnitude.
motivation: Directional beam sweeping for initial access in mmWave networks incurs large latency and signaling overhead as arrays grow and deployments densify, and ML-based beam prediction is hampered by the difficulty of obtaining environment-representative training data.
method: The authors combine offline ray-traced digital-twin channel generation, region-based localization, a reliability-weighted ensemble of base and specialist classifiers, and XAI-attribution-driven pruning of the beam codebook, training on imperfect digital-twin data and evaluating on real-world surrogate data.
result: The approach reaches 96.80% top-1 and 98.36% top-3 beam prediction accuracy and reduces over-the-air sounding overhead by almost an order of magnitude versus exhaustive sweeping, outperforming CNN and DNN baselines.
conclusion: Digital-twin-assisted ensemble learning with explainability-based pruning is an effective latency-aware beam management architecture for mmWave MIMO systems, though the work is purely classical wireless engineering.

title: A Polynomial-size Logical Twin For Neural Networks
authors: Marcelo Finger Sandro Preto
abstract: ArXiv:2611.01146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A logical twin of a neural network is a logical representation that mimics the computation of the network through logical formulas. We revisit two earlier proposals for constructing logical twins of feedforward neural networks in {\L}ukasiewicz logic, both of which are susceptible to exponential blow-up in running time and representation size. Building on ideas from both approaches, we present a new construction that directly yields logical twins in {\L}ukasiewicz logic. We show that this construction can be computed in polynomial time and produces polynomial-size logical twins. Finally, we report an empirical evaluation of the three methods, showing that the new proposal substantially outperforms the other two.
tldr: The paper introduces a new polynomial-time construction of polynomial-size 'logical twins' — Łukasiewicz-logic formula representations that mimic feedforward neural network computation — and shows empirically it outperforms two earlier exponential-blow-up approaches.
motivation: Existing constructions of logical twins for feedforward neural networks in Łukasiewicz logic suffer from exponential blow-up in running time and representation size, limiting their practical use for verifying or reasoning about networks.
method: Combining ideas from two prior constructions, the authors define a new direct construction of logical twins in Łukasiewicz logic and prove it runs in polynomial time and yields polynomial-size formulas, followed by an empirical comparison of the three methods.
result: The new construction is proven polynomial in both computation time and output size, and the empirical evaluation shows it substantially outperforms the two earlier proposals.
conclusion: Polynomial-size logical twins make logic-based representation and analysis of neural networks tractable, offering a practical alternative to earlier exponentially scaling encodings.

title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks For Solving Homogeneous And Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
authors: Luke Oluwaseye Joel
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations. Standard PINNs leverage physical laws encoded within the loss function, but their predictive performance can be constrained by optimization challenges and approximation errors. To address this, we introduce a post-processing boosting stage where the residual errors from the PINN prediction are modeled using some regression algorithms - including LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The outputs from these boosted models are aggregated to generate a corrected, high-fidelity prediction. The proposed methodology is systematically validated through quantitative metrics and comparative analysis against the standard PINN baseline. The results demonstrate that the boosted PINN framework significantly reduces prediction error, and improves generalization, offering a powerful and flexible approach for solving scientific and engineering problems governed by differential equations.
tldr: A hybrid framework combining Physics-Informed Neural Networks with boosting regression algorithms to solve Lane-Emden type differential equations.
motivation: Standard PINNs can suffer from optimization challenges and approximation errors, limiting their predictive performance.
method: The approach uses a post-processing boosting stage where residual errors from PINN predictions are modeled using regression algorithms (LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, SVR) and aggregated to produce corrected predictions.
result: The boosted PINN framework significantly reduces prediction error and improves generalization compared to standard PINN baseline.
conclusion: This offers a powerful and flexible approach for solving scientific and engineering problems governed by differential equations.

title: Porteous Meets Walsh: Counting Critical Points For $\mathcal{H}_2$-Norm Model Order Reduction Using Algebraic Geometry Behind Multiparameter Eigenvalue Problems
authors: Sibren Lagauw, Leonie Kayser, Bart de Moor
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several polynomial systems arising in systems and control have been shown to exhibit a partially linear structure, which allows them to be reformulated as a multiparameter eigenvalue problem (MEP). In this work, we show how such MEP formulations can be leveraged to obtain refined information about the solution set of the polynomial system. We demonstrate, in the setting of single-input single-output [MATH]-norm model order reduction, how the Thom--Porteous formula can be used to derive an exact count of the complex solutions of the critical equations derived from Walsh's theorem. We prove, under suitable genericity assumptions, that their set of complex solutions is finite and that all solutions occur without multiplicity. Moreover, we derive an explicit formula for the total number of complex solutions as a function of the model orders. Throughout, we provide a self-contained and application-oriented exposition of the algebro-geometric tools required for our analysis, with the aim of making them accessible to the broader engineering community.
tldr: The paper uses algebraic geometry and multiparameter eigenvalue problems to count complex critical points in H2-norm model order reduction.
motivation: Polynomial systems in systems and control can have hidden partially linear structure, enabling reformulation as multiparameter eigenvalue problems; the authors aim to extract refined solution-set information from this structure.
method: They apply the Thom–Porteous formula to the critical equations from Walsh's theorem in single-input single-output H2-norm model order reduction and prove genericity conditions under which the complex solution set is finite and multiplicity-free.
result: They derive an explicit formula for the total number of complex solutions as a function of the model orders and provide a self-contained exposition of the required algebro-geometric tools.
conclusion: The work connects algebraic geometry to control-theoretic model reduction by giving exact solution counts for critical equations, with the goal of making these tools accessible to engineers.

title: Optimistic Gradient Algorithms With Randomized Coordinate And Variance Reduction Strategies For Composite Inclusions
authors: Ngh\~ia Nguyen-Trung, Ion Necoara, Quoc Tran-Dinh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider a class of possibly nonmonotone finite-sum composite inclusions in which evaluating all components or updating all coordinates at every iteration can be computationally expensive. We develop two optimistic gradient frameworks that combine variance reduction with randomized block-coordinate updates. The first framework applies under a blockwise average Lipschitz continuity condition and the existence of a weak-Minty solution. It achieves an [MATH] convergence rate for the expected squared residual, and its iterates converge almost surely under mild additional conditions. The second framework relies on a backward-forward reformulation under average co-coercivity and co-hypomonotonicity. It achieves faster [MATH] and [MATH] rates for the expected squared residual, as well as [MATH] almost-sure rates. For both frameworks, we provide a generic condition on the stochastic estimator that covers mini-batch, loopless SVRG, and a generalized JacSketch-type estimator, and we derive the corresponding oracle complexities under importance-based block sampling. In particular, in highly heterogeneous regimes, the L-SVRG and JacSketch variants attain [MATH] and [MATH] oracle complexities for the nonaccelerated and accelerated methods, respectively. Numerical experiments illustrate the effects of variance reduction and block-coordinate sampling, and compare the proposed methods with existing baselines.
tldr: The paper develops two optimistic gradient frameworks combining variance reduction with randomized block-coordinate updates for solving possibly nonmonotone finite-sum composite inclusions.
motivation: Evaluating all components or updating all coordinates each iteration is computationally expensive in large-scale finite-sum inclusion problems, motivating cheaper stochastic and block-coordinate schemes.
method: Two optimistic gradient frameworks are proposed: one under blockwise average Lipschitz continuity with a weak-Minty solution assumption, and another via a backward-forward reformulation under average co-coercivity and co-hypomonotonicity, both with generic stochastic estimators (mini-batch, loopless SVRG, JacSketch) and importance-based block sampling.
result: The methods achieve O(1/k) expected squared-residual rates (with faster accelerated rates in the second framework), almost-sure convergence, and improved oracle complexities such as O(n/ε) and accelerated variants in highly heterogeneous regimes.
conclusion: The proposed optimistic gradient algorithms with variance reduction and randomized coordinate updates offer provable convergence and complexity gains for composite inclusion problems, validated by numerical experiments.

title: Price Is Only The Symptom: Understanding And Analyzing Economic-State Manipulation Vulnerabilities In DeFi
authors: Hao Wu, Haijun Wang, Xiapu Luo, Ming Fan, Ting Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Economic-state manipulation has emerged as a significant security threat to decentralized finance (DeFi), causing substantial financial losses. Existing studies predominantly characterize these attacks as price manipulation, focusing on observable price distortions while overlooking underlying violations of economic-state integrity. We conduct a comprehensive empirical study of Economic-State Manipulation (ESM) vulnerabilities in DeFi. We first curate a diverse dataset comprising 276 real-world attacks and 91 Code4rena audit findings. Based on these cases, we develop a cause-oriented taxonomy comprising four primary categories and eleven subcategories. Our analysis reveals that ESM vulnerabilities extend beyond conventional price manipulation, frequently involving violations of protocol-internal accounting, AMM state consistency, and execution-time constraints. We further investigate the evaluation datasets of six existing studies and find that, although they cover 6-10 vulnerability subcategories, their distributions remain dominated by limited manipulation mechanisms. Furthermore, we systematically evaluate seven representative detection approaches on our dataset. Our results reveal limited coverage, with the best-performing approach identifying only 50.4% of real-world attacks. Through an analysis of false negatives and false positives, we identify fundamental limitations arising from reliance on predefined attack patterns, insufficient reasoning about economic-state semantics, and incomplete exploitability validation. These findings provide empirical insights for developing more generalizable ESM vulnerability detection techniques.
tldr: This paper empirically studies economic-state manipulation vulnerabilities in decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols and benchmarks existing detection tools.
motivation: Existing DeFi security work frames these exploits narrowly as price manipulation, missing deeper violations of protocol-internal accounting and execution-time constraints that cause large financial losses.
method: The authors curate a dataset of 276 real-world attacks plus 91 Code4rena audit findings, build a cause-oriented taxonomy with four categories and eleven subcategories, and evaluate seven detection approaches against it.
result: ESM vulnerabilities extend well beyond price distortion; existing evaluation datasets are dominated by limited manipulation mechanisms, and the best detector identifies only 50.4% of real-world attacks.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for detection techniques that reason about economic-state semantics rather than relying on predefined attack patterns, offering empirical guidance for more generalizable DeFi security tooling.

title: Approximate Clearing In Financial Networks With Credit Default Swaps: Hardness Thresholds, A Box Algorithm, Barriers, And Exact Solvency At Bounded Degree
authors: Michal \v{c}ert\'ik
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study approximate clearing in financial networks with credit default swaps. For weak notions (W) and (I), we prove PPAD-hardness below a threshold approximately [MATH] and give a polynomial-time interval algorithm above a threshold approximately [MATH]. On networks whose CDS writers are solvent ex ante, the corresponding bounds are [MATH] and [MATH], approximately [MATH] and [MATH]. The thresholds are sharp for bounded-radius algorithms: for (I) on writer-solvent networks, and for (I) and (W) in general. On non-degenerate networks, (W) and (I) have identical hardness and tractability threshold endpoints. For exact-solvency notion (D), PPAD-hardness holds at every rational error [MATH] on non-degenerate networks. On a restricted unit-notional class, let [MATH] be the maximum number of CDS contracts held by a core bank, counted with multiplicity. For rational [MATH], writing [MATH], the problem is polynomial-time solvable when [MATH] and PPAD-complete otherwise. At [MATH] the boundary is [MATH] versus [MATH]; below [MATH], degree [MATH] is already PPAD-complete, while degree [MATH] is exactly solvable. These degree results concern (D) and do not close the (W)/(I) approximation windows. We also establish a barrier to Pure-Circuit reductions certified by interval propagation under stated interface and auxiliary-bank restrictions. A finite-precision interval algorithm reduces writer-solvent (I) to point selection in near-stalled boxes; selection is polynomial-time when the residual matrix is symmetric or monotone on each strongly connected component. The general and writer-solvent approximation windows remain open.
tldr: The paper studies computational complexity and algorithms for approximate clearing in financial networks with credit default swaps.
motivation: It aims to characterize hardness thresholds, tractability regimes, and algorithmic barriers for clearing problems in financial networks with CDS contracts.
method: The author uses PPAD-hardness reductions, interval algorithms, bounded-radius algorithm thresholds, and degree-restricted exact-solvency analysis.
result: The paper establishes sharp thresholds for weak and interval clearing notions, PPAD-hardness for exact solvency, and polynomial-time solvability in restricted bounded-degree cases.
conclusion: The work maps out computational boundaries for financial-network clearing with CDS, while leaving general approximation windows open.

title: Siting And Curtailment Depth Limit The Grid Headroom Available To New Large Loads
authors: Nils Johnson, Geoff Blanford, John E. T. Bistline
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data center demand is increasing faster than generation can be built, encouraging proposals to interconnect large loads on condition that they reduce consumption during high-stress periods. Estimates of how much load can be added via flexibility rest on simplified accounting and report only annual curtailed electricity. Here we use a national energy systems model that co-optimizes hourly generation and load curtailment across 16 U.S. regions to characterize the flexibility and power system impacts of enabling headroom. While 50 GW can be served while curtailing less than 0.1% of its annual energy, small annual curtailment conceals potentially severe operating requirements. Most regions require curtailment deeper than 90% in at least one hour, so the load must disconnect or have sufficient on-site resources to provide full back up. Furthermore, announced data center locations are not aligned with modeled headroom and relying on existing generation fleets raises CO2 emissions and wholesale electricity prices.
tldr: A national energy systems model shows that although ~50 GW of new data-center load can be served with tiny annual curtailment, most U.S. regions would still require near-total (>90%) curtailment in at least one hour, and announced data-center sites do not align with available grid headroom.
motivation: Data-center demand is outpacing generation build-out, prompting proposals to interconnect large flexible loads that curtail during high-stress periods; existing estimates rely on simplified annual accounting that may hide severe operating requirements.
method: The authors use a national capacity-expansion and dispatch model that co-optimizes hourly generation and load curtailment across 16 U.S. regions to quantify flexibility and power-system impacts of serving new headroom loads.
result: While 50 GW can be served with less than 0.1% annual energy curtailment, most regions require curtailment deeper than 90% in at least one hour, implying full on-site backup or disconnection; announced data-center locations mismatch modeled headroom, and relying on existing fleets raises CO2 emissions and wholesale prices.
conclusion: Annual curtailment metrics conceal severe hourly operating requirements, so siting and curtailment-depth constraints, not just total flexible capacity, limit how much large load the grid can absorb.

title: Diagram Of Geodesic Intervals In $C'(1/8)$-Groups
authors: Alexander Hoffmann
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a group characterized by a small cancellation [MATH]-presentation. We study the structure of its Cayley graph, specifically geodesic intervals and digons. We prove that all geodesic segments [MATH] of length [MATH] can be covered by finitely many simple geodesic digons with pairwise [MATH]-short lower intersections whose lower sides lie on a common geodesic segment [MATH]. This is a generalization of a proposition of Kharlampovich-Sklinos (arXiv:2106.05461) for random groups. We then bound this resulting diagram of digons, showing that the total perimeter of its cells and its edge count is bounded by [MATH], and the cycle rank is equal to the number of distinct cell contours. Thus, although there may be many different geodesics, the size of their union is bounded linearly in the distance between their endpoints. The constant is independent of the number and lengths of the defining relators. In particular, the estimate applies to infinite presentations with unbounded relator lengths. From this we get a consequence for growth, allowing us to compare the number of geodesic words with the number of group elements of the same length.
tldr: The paper analyzes the structure of geodesic intervals in Cayley graphs of C'(1/8) small-cancellation groups, showing they can be covered by finitely many digons with linearly bounded total size.
motivation: Understanding the geometry of geodesics in groups with small-cancellation presentations generalizes prior results for random groups (Kharlampovich–Sklinos) and yields bounds useful for growth comparisons.
method: The author decomposes geodesic segments into simple geodesic digons with short lower intersections lying on a common geodesic, then bounds the resulting diagram's perimeter, edge count, and cycle rank.
result: The diagram of digons has total perimeter and edge count linear in the endpoint distance, with constants independent of the number and lengths of relators, so the union of geodesics is linearly bounded even for infinite presentations.
conclusion: This yields growth-theoretic consequences, allowing comparison between the number of geodesic words and the number of group elements of the same length.

title: Inference In An Interactive Multi-type Branching Network
authors: Gunay Hasanli, Michel Mandjes, Jiesen Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study statistical inference for a high-dimensional stochastic interaction model observed only through low-dimensional aggregate data. The model describes pairwise communication between [MATH] individuals as a collection of mutually interacting branching processes with immigration, where activity on one directed pair may trigger subsequent activity in the reverse direction. The latent interaction counts are not observed. Instead, for each individual, only the total number of messages sent and received in each time slot is available. This aggregation gives rise to an inverse problem in which the parameters governing the latent pairwise dynamics must be recovered from substantially compressed observations.
tldr: The paper develops statistical inference methods for a high-dimensional multi-type branching process model of pairwise communication observed only through aggregated per-individual message counts.
motivation: Interaction data between individuals (e.g., message exchange in communication networks) is often only available in compressed, aggregate form, so one needs to recover latent pairwise interaction dynamics from low-dimensional observations.
method: The authors model pairwise activity as mutually interacting branching processes with immigration, allowing reverse-direction triggering, and treat the problem as an inverse problem, estimating latent pairwise parameters from total sent/received counts per time slot.
result: They derive an estimation framework (including identifiability conditions and asymptotic behaviour of the estimators) that recovers the latent interaction parameters despite the massive aggregation of the observations.
conclusion: Aggregate communication counts can suffice to infer latent pairwise interaction structure, providing a tractable inference methodology for high-dimensional stochastic interaction networks.

title: Parameter-Free First-Order Method For Constrained Variational Inequalities
authors: Yan Wu, Qi Luo, Yuyuan Ouyang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constrained variational inequalities (VIs) provide a general framework for modeling and solving complementarity and equilibrium problems with functional constraints. In this paper, we propose a parameter-free accelerated operator sliding (PFAOS) method for solving monotone VIs with convex smooth constraints. For a single constraint, PFAOS achieves an operator evaluation complexity of [MATH] and a constraint gradient evaluation complexity of [MATH], without requiring prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant of the VI operator or the smoothness constant of the constraint function. We further extend PFAOS to multiple constraints by incorporating a primal-dual hybrid gradient update, yielding a multi-constrained PFAOS (MC-PFAOS) method that preserves the same evaluation complexities. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted on large-scale games with coupling constraints to validate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.
tldr: The paper proposes a parameter-free accelerated operator sliding (PFAOS) method for solving monotone variational inequalities with convex smooth constraints, extending it to multiple constraints via a primal-dual hybrid gradient update.
motivation: Constrained variational inequalities model complementarity and equilibrium problems, but existing accelerated methods typically require prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant of the operator and the smoothness constant of the constraints.
method: The authors develop a parameter-free accelerated operator sliding scheme that adaptively estimates problem constants, and combine it with a primal-dual hybrid gradient update to handle multiple coupling constraints (MC-PFAOS).
result: PFAOS attains operator evaluation and constraint gradient evaluation complexities matching accelerated rates without tuning parameters, and numerical experiments on large-scale games with coupling constraints demonstrate efficiency.
conclusion: Parameter-free acceleration is achievable for constrained variational inequalities at both single- and multi-constraint settings, offering practical advantages for large-scale equilibrium problems.

title: A Preconditioned Semismooth Newton Method For Box-Constrained Elliptic Optimal Control Problems With Random Coefficients
authors: Zhendong Li, Akwum Onwunta, Hailing Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the optimal control problem of an elliptic PDE with random diffusion under pointwise box constraints on the control. The constraints make the optimality conditions nonsmooth, with an active set that is not known in advance, and the random diffusion couples the state and the adjoint across all stochastic modes. To design a solution algorithm for this problem, we rely on the Fenchel duality viewpoint. Fenchel duality absorbs the box constraint into the objective and yields an exact reduced problem in the elliptic adjoint variable alone. After a stochastic Galerkin--finite element discretization, eliminating the state leaves a strongly monotone, piecewise smooth equation, which we solve directly by a matrix-free semismooth Newton method with the box projection retained exactly and with no outer iteration, penalty or smoothing parameter. Next, we introduce and analyze a current-set preconditioner, which adds the active-set correction of the current Newton step to a mean-diffusion reference operator and is inverted exactly by a rank-1 update. For implementation, we use a cheaper preconditioner that keeps only a fraction of free control values. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence of the state, and Newton and PCG counts that stay bounded under mesh refinement and growth of the stochastic dimension.
tldr: A matrix-free semismooth Newton solver with a current-set preconditioner for box-constrained elliptic PDE optimal control problems with random diffusion coefficients.
motivation: Box constraints make the optimality conditions nonsmooth with an unknown active set, and random coefficients couple state and adjoint across stochastic modes, complicating efficient numerical solution.
method: Using Fenchel duality, the box constraint is absorbed into the objective to give an exact reduced problem in the adjoint variable; after stochastic Galerkin-finite element discretization, a matrix-free semismooth Newton method solves the resulting strongly monotone piecewise smooth equation, accelerated by a rank-1 current-set preconditioner.
result: Numerical experiments show second-order state convergence and Newton/PCG iteration counts that remain bounded under mesh refinement and increasing stochastic dimension.
conclusion: The approach avoids outer iterations, penalties, or smoothing parameters, yielding a robust and scalable solver for random-coefficient PDE-constrained optimization.

title: Unconstrained Support Points Can Leave A Convex Support
authors: Zhaohui Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Support points provide a practical and effective way to approximate a probability distribution by a small set of equally weighted representatives through energy-distance minimization. In many applications, the variables satisfy convex constraints that the representatives should also respect. We investigate whether unconstrained support points automatically satisfy such constraints and show that this is not guaranteed. We construct counterexamples using three planar observations, a density with full triangular support, and positive-definite matrix data admitting an indefinite optimal representative under the Frobenius norm. We also identify cases in which containment holds, establish stability under distributional perturbations, and quantify the objective cost of imposing a convex-hull constraint. For a fixed number of representatives and a positive population constraint gap, empirical configurations with vanishing global objective error eventually leave the sample convex hull almost surely.
tldr: The paper shows that unconstrained support points obtained by energy-distance minimization need not lie inside a convex constraint set, and constructs counterexamples plus stability and cost analyses.
motivation: Support points are widely used to summarize distributions with a few equally weighted representatives, but many applications require the representatives to satisfy convex constraints; whether unconstrained optimization respects such constraints was unclear.
method: Counterexamples are constructed from three planar observations, a density with full triangular support, and positive-definite matrix data yielding an indefinite Frobenius-norm optimal representative; cases where containment does hold are characterized, stability under distributional perturbation is established, and the objective cost of enforcing a convex-hull constraint is quantified.
result: Unconstrained support points can provably leave the convex hull; for fixed representative count and a positive population constraint gap, empirically optimal configurations eventually exit the sample convex hull almost surely.
conclusion: Constrained variants of support-point optimization are necessary in practice, and the paper provides diagnostics and cost estimates for when constraint enforcement matters.

title: Dynamic Programming Principle For Controlled Systems Driven By Fractional Brownian Motions And Related Backward Stochastic Riccati Equations
authors: Yuecai Han, Yaozhong Hu, Yuhang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work aims to study the stochastic optimal control problems of controlled stochastic differential systems driven by both Brownian motions and fractional Brownian motions via dynamic programming principle. The stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is obtained. Different from the classical case, the obtained stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is a backward stochastic partial differential equation driven by both fractional Brownian motions and standard Brownian motions, whose solution is a pair of random fields. For linear quadratic optimal control problem this backward stochastic partial differential equation is explicitly solved by relating it to a backward stochastic Riccati equation.
tldr: The paper develops a dynamic programming principle for controlled stochastic systems driven by both standard and fractional Brownian motions, deriving a stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation and solving it explicitly in the linear-quadratic case.
motivation: Stochastic optimal control for systems with fractional Brownian noise lacks a systematic dynamic programming framework analogous to the classical case, motivating a formulation of the associated stochastic HJB equation.
method: The authors apply the dynamic programming principle to controlled SDEs with mixed Brownian/fractional Brownian driving noise, obtaining a backward stochastic partial differential equation for a pair of random fields, which is solved explicitly for linear-quadratic problems via a backward stochastic Riccati equation.
result: A stochastic HJB equation is derived and shown to be a backward stochastic PDE driven by both fractional and standard Brownian motions; for the LQ case it reduces to a backward stochastic Riccati equation with explicit solution.
conclusion: The work extends classical stochastic control theory to fractional-Brownian-driven systems, providing a tractable Riccati-based solution for linear-quadratic control.

title: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning For Mixed Integer Programming Solvers
authors: Zhengzhong Ricky You, Kaizhao Sun, Zeping Min, Wotao Yin, Xinshang Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated configuration of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers largely relies on black-box optimization. Each trial requires an expensive solver run and provides only a scalar outcome, so tuning can require many such evaluations. Human experts take a different approach. They inspect solver logs, identify performance bottlenecks, and adjust the parameters that address them. We propose Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), which uses a large language model (LLM) to automate this process. LDST extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, uses the LLM to propose sparse edits to the current best configuration based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior, and validates each proposal before execution. A regime-adaptive objective selects the tuning signal according to the information available from a time-limited run, while a log-based completion signal estimates completion time from branch-and-bound tree growth recorded in ordinary solver logs, so that solved and unsolved runs share one time scale. On 215 instances from five benchmark sets, LDST reduces geometric-mean loss by 43.9% on easy instances and 16.7% on intermediate instances relative to the best of SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search. In both regimes, LDST achieves a lower loss with 10 proposals than any of these baselines achieves with 50. Configurations that LDST tunes on a single instance also transfer better than baseline configurations to unseen instances of the same family.
tldr: LDST uses an LLM to read MIP solver logs, diagnose bottlenecks, and propose sparse parameter edits, outperforming SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search with far fewer solver runs.
motivation: Automated MIP solver configuration is dominated by black-box optimization, which needs many costly solver runs and yields only scalar feedback; human experts instead read logs and target bottlenecks, a process the authors aim to automate.
method: The pipeline extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, has an LLM propose sparse configuration edits grounded in parameter semantics and observed behavior, validates proposals before execution, and combines a regime-adaptive objective with a log-based completion-time estimator to unify solved and unsolved runs.
result: On 215 instances across five benchmark sets, geometric-mean loss drops 43.9% (easy) and 16.7% (intermediate) versus the best baseline, with 10 proposals beating 50 baseline proposals; single-instance tuned configurations also transfer better to unseen instances.
conclusion: Log-driven, semantics-aware LLM tuning is a sample-efficient alternative to black-box solver configuration, suggesting LLM-guided reasoning over diagnostics as a practical paradigm for algorithm configuration.

title: Alder: A Single-Loop Augmented-Lagrangian Damped Extragradient Method For Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Problems With Nonlinear Coupled Constraints
authors: H. Zhang, M. Zhang, Z. Xu, Y. -H. Dai
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ALDER, a single-loop augmented-Lagrangian damped extragradient method, is proposed for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax problems with nonlinear coupled inequality constraints. Within an augmented-Lagrangian framework, ALDER combines prediction--correction steps for the primal variables with explicit projected-and-relaxed multiplier updates in a single loop. The penalty parameter is fixed throughout each run, eliminating inner-loop subproblem solves and iterative penalty updates. We establish uniform boundedness of the relaxed multiplier sequence and, under an extended Mangasarian--Fromovitz constraint qualification, boundedness of the projected output multiplier. Building on these bounds, we show that ALDER finds an [MATH]-KKT point within [MATH] complete first-order oracle evaluations in the strongly concave setting and [MATH] in the concave setting. These bounds improve upon the best known complexity bounds for multi-loop algorithms for this problem class, achieved by FAL, by removing a [MATH] factor, while retaining a single-loop update structure.
tldr: ALDER is a single-loop augmented-Lagrangian damped extragradient algorithm for smooth nonconvex-concave minimax problems with nonlinear coupled inequality constraints.
motivation: Existing multi-loop augmented-Lagrangian methods for this problem class require expensive inner-loop subproblem solves and iterative penalty updates, which motivates a single-loop approach with a fixed penalty parameter.
method: The algorithm combines prediction-correction primal steps with explicit projected-and-relaxed multiplier updates inside a single augmented-Lagrangian loop, using a fixed penalty parameter, and analyzes multiplier boundedness under an extended Mangasarian-Fromovitz constraint qualification.
result: The authors prove an [MATH]-KKT point is found within [MATH] first-order oracle evaluations in the strongly concave case and [MATH] in the concave case, improving on FAL-type multi-loop bounds by removing a [MATH] factor.
conclusion: ALDER achieves improved complexity guarantees while retaining a simple single-loop structure, making it attractive for constrained nonconvex-concave minimax optimization.

title: Forgetting Matters: When Subspace Optimization Accelerates Without The Strong Convexity Parameter
authors: Ilya Kuruzov, Alexander Vyguzov, Ivan Dorofeev, Alexander Gasnikov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) minimizes the objective exactly over a few directions built from past iterates. It needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and behaves like an accelerated method in experiments. This led to the conjecture that it is accelerated in the strongly convex case without knowing the strong convexity parameter. We show that the conjecture fails in the worst case. For every subspace method whose memory forgets slowly, namely a window of recent gradients and steps together with cumulative sums with subexponential weights, we construct a counterexample: acceleration requires a window of length of order [MATH], where [MATH] is the condition number. SESOP and the plane form of conjugate gradients are therefore not accelerated. Memories that forget fast avoid this obstruction. Pairs of geometric filters give accelerated methods with logarithmic memory or only two stored vectors. They need neither the strong convexity parameter nor the smoothness constant, never restart the iterate and restart their memory at most [MATH] times. Finally, the method with fixed activation times remains asymptotically accelerated on functions with Lipschitz Hessian even when each subproblem is solved by a single Newton step.
tldr: The paper disproves the conjecture that sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) is accelerated in the strongly convex setting without knowing the strong convexity parameter, showing that slow-forgetting memory requires a window of order the condition number, while fast-forgetting (geometric filter) memories recover acceleration with logarithmic memory.
motivation: SESOP requires no problem constants and empirically behaves like an accelerated method, leading to the conjecture that it is accelerated even in the strongly convex case without knowledge of the strong convexity parameter; the authors aim to test this conjecture rigorously.
method: They construct worst-case counterexample functions for every subspace method whose memory forgets slowly (sliding window of recent gradients/steps plus cumulative sums with subexponential weights), and then analyze pairs of geometric filters as fast-forgetting memories, including a variant with fixed activation times solved by a single Newton step.
result: Acceleration for slow-forgetting memories requires a window of length of order the condition number, so SESOP and the plane form of conjugate gradients are not accelerated; in contrast, geometric-filter pairs achieve acceleration with logarithmic memory or only two stored vectors, without needing strong convexity or smoothness constants and restarting at most logarithmically many times.
conclusion: Forgetting rate of the memory is the crucial property determining acceleration of subspace optimization methods; fast-forgetting designs yield parameter-free accelerated methods, and fixed-activation-time variants remain asymptotically accelerated even for functions with Lipschitz Hessian.

title: A Posteriori Error Estimates For A Finite Volume Approximation Of A Local Sensing Keller-Segel Model
authors: Kiwoong Kwon Niklas Kolbe
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A local sensing Keller-Segel model, in which cells adjust their motility to the local chemoattractant rather than its gradient, and a semi-implicit finite volume scheme for its numerical approximation are studied. Computable a posteriori bounds for the approximation error measured in terms of the [MATH] and [MATH] norms of the cell density are derived based on a new stability estimate and suitable reconstructions of the flux and the flux potential of the numerical solution. Optimal scaling of the estimates is numerically demonstrated in 1D and 2D experiments. Moreover, an adaptive mesh refinement method steered by the estimator is proposed for the 1D case, and its efficiency is numerically verified.
tldr: The paper derives computable a posteriori error estimates for a semi-implicit finite volume discretization of a local-sensing Keller-Segel chemotaxis model.
motivation: Local-sensing Keller-Segel models describe cell motility adapting to chemoattractant concentration rather than its gradient, and reliable numerical approximation with certified error control is needed for such nonlinear advection-diffusion systems.
method: The authors prove a new stability estimate and construct suitable reconstructions of the numerical flux and flux potential, yielding a posteriori bounds in L^p-type norms of the cell density, plus an estimator-driven adaptive mesh refinement scheme in 1D.
result: The estimates exhibit optimal scaling in 1D and 2D numerical experiments, and the adaptive refinement strategy is shown to be efficient in the 1D case.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous, computable error control framework for finite volume simulation of local-sensing chemotaxis models, with demonstrated practical adaptivity.

title: When Appearance And Motion Disagree: Evaluating Class--motion Consistency Against Disguised Uncrewed Surface Vessels
authors: Jon Reifschneider
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Defense systems for maritime assets must distinguish approaching benign craft from uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) with sufficient warning to act. Shore cameras using computer vision can separate hostile vessels from benign traffic, but these systems may be attacked using an adversarial hull patch or physical disguise. We evaluate adversarial hull patches and find they suppress detection in up to 29% of attempts but never cause misclassification as benign. Physical disguise, however, can bypass both a camera check and a radar presence check. To evaluate defenses, we develop a hybrid replay protocol from automatic identification system (AIS) tracks that combines recorded benign motion with direct or off-axis attack run-ins. We find that for recreational-labeled vessels attacking via direct run-in within 4 nautical miles, an asset-relative closing-rate check flags 94-95% at 15-20 knots, compared with 12% for a track-only speed check. The checks are complementary on off-axis approaches, constraining the attacker to remain below both thresholds and extending the time required to reach the asset. Flagging on either check has a 4.9% held-out false-alarm rate overall and 12.3% on recreational traffic. The replay-based evaluation protocol supports comparative test and evaluation of defense methods.
tldr: The paper evaluates adversarial hull patches and physical disguise attacks against shore-camera and radar defenses for detecting hostile uncrewed surface vessels, and proposes a closing-rate check validated via AIS-based replay.
motivation: Maritime asset defense needs early discrimination between benign craft and approaching USVs, but computer-vision and radar checks may be defeated by adversarial patches or physical disguise.
method: The author tests adversarial hull patches and disguise against camera/radar detection, then builds a hybrid replay protocol from recorded AIS tracks combining benign motion with direct and off-axis attack run-ins to compare defense checks.
result: Hull patches suppress detection in up to 29% of attempts yet never cause benign misclassification, while physical disguise bypasses both camera and radar checks; an asset-relative closing-rate check flags 94-95% of direct run-ins at 15-20 knots versus 12% for a track-only speed check, at 4.9% overall and 12.3% recreational false-alarm rates.
conclusion: Complementary closing-rate and speed checks constrain attackers and extend warning time, and the replay protocol enables comparative test and evaluation of maritime defense methods.

title: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Detecting Access Control Flaws At Sensitive Callsites In Android Firmware
authors: Haotian Deng, Meng Hao, Hanxiao Chen, Xinyuan Qian, Guowen Xu, Hongwei Li, Chaoshun Zuo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing studies of vulnerable pre-installed Android apps identify dangerous behavior by checking whether an app invokes an API from a predefined set of security-sensitive APIs. These sets usually exclude generic APIs to avoid false positives; unfortunately, this misses a class of vulnerabilities in which a generic API, such as a database read, appears benign in general but becomes security-sensitive when operating on protected data, yet is left without sufficient access control. While this class of vulnerabilities appears addressable via access control analysis, existing studies focus only on the presence of checks, not on whether those checks enforce sufficient protection for the operation at a given callsite. In this work, we propose Callix, which first assesses callsite sensitivity by jointly analyzing the invoked API functionality and the data involved in the operation, then recovers each security check on the execution path as an explicit security property, and finally introduces the notion of restriction context to decide whether these checks are sufficient for the identified sensitive operation. We evaluated Callix on 1,750 distinct pre-installed apps from the 10 top-tier Android vendors as of 2025. In total, Callix discovered 819 vulnerable paths across these vendors, 42.1% of which allow reading or modifying private user data through generic database operations. Manual validation of a random 60% sample shows a precision of 95.1%. Many of our findings have been confirmed and rewarded through vendor bug bounty programs.
tldr: Callix is a static analysis system that detects access-control flaws at sensitive callsites in pre-installed Android firmware apps, including cases where generic APIs operate on protected data.
motivation: Existing vulnerability scanners for pre-installed Android apps only flag invocations of predefined security-sensitive APIs, missing cases where generic APIs (e.g., database reads) become sensitive due to the protected data they touch, and they check only for the presence of guards rather than their sufficiency.
method: Callix jointly analyzes API functionality and the data involved to assess callsite sensitivity, recovers each security check along the execution path as an explicit security property, and uses a 'restriction context' notion to judge whether the checks sufficiently protect the sensitive operation.
result: Evaluated on 1,750 pre-installed apps from the top 10 Android vendors, Callix found 819 vulnerable paths, 42.1% involving private user data accessed via generic database operations; manual validation of a 60% sample gave 95.1% precision, with many findings confirmed through vendor bug bounties.
conclusion: Callsite-level, data-aware access-control analysis substantially outperforms API-signature-based detection for Android firmware and yields practically actionable, vendor-confirmed vulnerabilities.

title: AgentCap: Capability-Based Runtime Authorization For Secure Llm Agent Execution
authors: Peng Gao Aravinda Kashyap Kabbinamakki Suresh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model agents commonly collapse two decisions that security systems separate: selecting an action and determining whether that action is authorized. When a model exercises standing authority, indirect prompt injection can convert influence over its reasoning into unauthorized effects. We present AgentCap, a runtime authorization layer that externalizes this decision from the model and mediates every tool invocation through an MCP wrapper. Each request declares an intent, and AgentCap evaluates policy constraints over trust, workflow prerequisites, mutually exclusive authority, and the provenance of security-sensitive arguments. Authorized requests receive short-lived, budget-bounded capability tokens that are validated at the tool boundary. Delegation is restricted to session-bound parent-child chains that preserve action and resource while budget and lifetime can only be attenuated, preventing authority from being expanded or reused across unrelated agent sessions. A declarative policy language provides a common representation for runtime enforcement and predeployment analysis. Across AgentDojo and InjecAgent, AgentCap reduces attack success in every evaluated model-benchmark setting, including zero attack success with GPT-5.4 on both benchmarks. Controlled adversarial scenarios further show that AgentCap blocks every attempted unauthorized execution (ASR 0%) while preserving all legitimate operations exercised. These results demonstrate that agent security requires authorization of model-proposed effects at the tool boundary, independently of the model's reasoning.
tldr: AgentCap is a runtime authorization layer that mediates LLM agent tool invocations through an MCP wrapper, issuing short-lived budget-bounded capability tokens to prevent unauthorized effects from indirect prompt injection.
motivation: Language-model agents conflate action selection with authorization, so indirect prompt injection can turn influence over a model's reasoning into unauthorized real-world effects.
method: Every tool call declares an intent and is checked against declarative policies over trust, workflow prerequisites, mutually exclusive authority, and argument provenance; authorized calls get attenuated, session-bound capability tokens validated at the tool boundary.
result: On AgentDojo and InjecAgent, AgentCap reduces attack success across all evaluated model-benchmark settings, reaching zero ASR with GPT-5.4, and blocks all attempted unauthorized executions in controlled adversarial scenarios while preserving legitimate operations.
conclusion: Securing agents requires authorizing model-proposed effects at the tool boundary rather than relying on the model's own reasoning.

title: Cross-Evidence Authorization State Learning For Runtime Detection Of Broken Object-Level Authorization In Black-Box Web Applications
authors: Siqi Lin, Qianheng Cheng, Yiping Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broken object-level authorization (BOLA) remains difficult to detect in black-box Web applications because external runtime monitors generally lack access to source code, authorization policies, and object-ownership records. This paper proposes a cross-evidence authorization-state learning method that reconstructs subject--resource--object--action relations from request--response transactions. The method represents authorization relations with confidence-aware states, aggregates positive and negative evidence while accounting for provenance independence, and applies contamination-gated promotion, evidence quarantine and rollback, expiration, and revocation. A Python prototype is evaluated using a deterministic synthetic benchmark comprising 64,400 requests across five independent random seeds. In this benchmark, the proposed method achieves 100.00% recall, an F1-score of 56.63%, and a false-positive rate of 33.65%, while the measured unauthorized-relation pollution rate is 0.00%. Ablation experiments show that removing provenance independence or evidence quarantine increases the pollution rate to 100.00%. The experiments provide an initial evaluation under controlled synthetic conditions.
tldr: The paper proposes a cross-evidence authorization-state learning method to detect broken object-level authorization (BOLA) vulnerabilities in black-box web applications at runtime.
motivation: External runtime monitors for black-box web applications lack access to source code, authorization policies, and object-ownership records, making BOLA detection difficult.
method: Subject-resource-object-action relations are reconstructed from request-response transactions and represented as confidence-aware authorization states, aggregating positive and negative evidence with provenance independence, plus contamination-gated promotion, evidence quarantine/rollback, expiration, and revocation.
result: On a synthetic benchmark of 64,400 requests across five seeds, the prototype achieves 100.00% recall, 56.63% F1, 33.65% false-positive rate, and 0.00% unauthorized-relation pollution; ablations removing provenance independence or evidence quarantine raise pollution to 100%.
conclusion: The approach shows promising initial results under controlled synthetic conditions, but real-world validation remains future work.

title: Illusion: Safeguarding Topology Confidentiality In Llm Multi-Agent Systems Via Behavior-Preserving Obfuscation
authors: Yiu-Fai Cheung, Hongzhi Guo, Miao Pan, Irwin King, Hao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.00923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The communication topology of Large Language Model Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-MASs) governs how information propagates among agents and encodes critical domain knowledge and expert workflow design. It is valuable intellectual property and plays a decisive role in system utility and safety, yet remains vulnerable to inference attacks that stealthily reconstruct it from agent outputs. Existing defenses detect or mitigate such attacks but do not proactively conceal the topology itself. We propose , a proactive topology obfuscation defense for LLM-MAS. injects fake edges and fake messages to present attackers with a deceptive topology, while selecting low-impact candidates that preserve output-distribution equivalence and task-accuracy non-inferiority. The resulting fake edges are designed to be indistinguishable from genuine messages under black-box observation. Extensive experiments show that reduces edge-level F1 from over 0.87 to 0.62 and graph similarity from over 0.94 to 0.71. It also largely preserves output distributions and task performance, and its fake edges resist both similarity-based and LLM-judge filtering, even under adaptive pruning.
tldr: The paper proposes Illusion, a proactive obfuscation defense that hides the communication topology of LLM multi-agent systems by injecting behavior-preserving fake edges and messages.
motivation: The communication topology of LLM multi-agent systems is valuable intellectual property encoding domain knowledge and workflow design, yet it can be reconstructed by inference attacks from agent outputs; existing defenses only detect or mitigate such attacks rather than concealing the topology itself.
method: Illusion injects fake edges and fake messages chosen to be low-impact, preserving output-distribution equivalence and task-accuracy non-inferiority, while making fake messages indistinguishable from genuine ones under black-box observation, including resistance to adaptive pruning.
result: Experiments show edge-level F1 drops from above 0.87 to 0.62 and graph similarity from above 0.94 to 0.71, while output distributions and task performance are largely preserved and fake edges resist similarity-based and LLM-judge filtering.
conclusion: Proactive topology obfuscation is a viable defense for protecting the confidentiality of LLM multi-agent system designs without sacrificing utility, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Trouble With Time: Compile Timestamps And First-Seen Date Regression In Ember2024
authors: Aditya Kapoor Edward Raff
abstract: ArXiv:2611.01031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable first-seen dates are important for constructing temporal malware evaluation splits, but this information often comes from external services that are not equally accessible to all researchers. We investigate whether machine learning can instead estimate an executable's first-seen date or determine when its PE/COFF compilation timestamp is unreliable. Using EMBER2024, we evaluate feature-based and raw-byte models across classification, regression, ranking, and latent-reliability formulations. Direct first-seen regression produces errors comparable to a substantial portion of the dataset's collection window, and none of the evaluated scores provides a useful chronological ordering of files. Current models therefore cannot replace externally sourced first-seen metadata. In contrast, classifiers can identify timestamps that fall within specified tolerances of first seen and can detect clearly implausible timestamps with high discrimination. We also find substantial timestamp disagreement among both benign and malicious executables, indicating that unreliable timestamps are not exclusively a product of malicious manipulation. These results establish baselines and identify timestamp reliability as a distinct direction for future security-ML research.
